title: Observability baseline: structured logs, metrics, health, dashboards, alerting
body:
## Context
CandleViewer runs unattended while holding real positions; its failure modes are silent by default (a stale topic still renders a chart, a slow event loop still serves requests, an order stuck in `Unknown` looks like nothing at all). This epic builds the observability floor that every later epic's Definition of Done depends on — `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` makes metrics part of a module's DoD, and `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0014-observability.md` states plainly: *a module without metrics is not finished*.

Plan material:
- Roadmap train: `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §4.2 (E04, 26 pts, S02–S03), §4.3 exit criterion 10 ("Grafana shows ingestion rate, WS state, queue depth and API latency; a synthetic alert fires and is received").
- Architecture: `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §12 (Observability) is the authoritative metric catalogue, logging, tracing, dashboard and alert policy; §3 defines the per-module package / lifecycle / `health()` conventions this epic instruments, and §3.12 (API / WS Gateway) hosts the `/metrics`, `/healthz`, `/readyz` and build-info endpoints. (Note: `20-architecture.md` identifies modules by named section, not by M-numbered ids; the `M24` shorthand used in the roadmap §4.2 table has no counterpart in the architecture document and is therefore not used anywhere in this backlog.) See §12.
- ADR: `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0014-observability.md` (Prometheus + Grafana + Alertmanager, structlog JSON, OTel on exactly two paths, two alert severities, Loki deliberately deferred).
- User stories domain **OBS**: `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §28 — US-OBS-001..007.
- Security requirements SR-120…SR-126 (`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §6.9) and threat K1 (key material leaking into logs).
- Budgets: `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §2 and §5.1 stage allocation.

### Estimate reconciliation (roadmap 26 — engineering 29 — epic 46)
`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` line 104/187 sizes E04 at **26 pts**. That roadmap figure prices *engineering* scope only (the structlog / metrics / health / alerting / dashboard build). The three numbers reconcile as follows, with no scope missing or double-counted:

| Figure | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Roadmap allocation | 26 | Engineering build, as sized during roadmap planning. |
| Engineering children (`E04-K01`, `E04-T01..T07`, `E04-S01`, `E04-S02`) | 29 | The same scope, re-estimated at grooming: 29 vs 26 = **+11.5%**, inside the ±15 % tolerance of `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md`, so the roadmap train needs no re-baselining. |
| This epic's `estimate` field | 46 | Per the backlog schema an epic's estimate is the **sum of all children**, which additionally includes the discipline tickets the roadmap line never priced: design `E04-D01`+`E04-D02` (7), QA `E04-Q01`+`E04-Q02` (5) and security `E04-X01`+`E04-X02` (5) = 17. 29 + 17 = 46. |

The +3-point engineering delta is absorbed inside the S02–S03 window; no roadmap change is requested.

### Sprint-window reconciliation (roadmap S02–S03 vs scheduled tickets)
The roadmap window **S02–S03** is the *engineering build* window. Every engineering ticket (`E04-K01`, `E04-T01..T07`, `E04-S01`, `E04-S02`) plus `E04-X01` (threat model, must precede `E04-T01`) and `E04-Q01` (scripted test plan) sits inside it. Three tickets sit deliberately outside it, each carrying its own justification section:

| Ticket | Sprint | Why outside S02–S03 |
|---|---|---|
| `E04-D01` | Sprint 01 | Design must land **two sprints before** the consuming FE work (`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md`); consumers `E04-T04` / `E04-S01` are Sprint 03. Sprint 01 immediately precedes the train window. |
| `E04-Q02` | Sprint 04 | Exploratory QA + regression pack over **shipped** code that only exists at the end of Sprint 03; epic QA sign-off (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2) is by definition a post-build gate. |
| `E04-X02` | Sprint 04 | Security review / abuse cases / SAST rules over merged artefacts from `E04-T01..T06` and `E04-S02`; the R0 SAST/SCA/secrets gate (`30-release-roadmap.md` §4.4) is a milestone gate, not a sprint-internal one. |

Neither Sprint-04 ticket consumes S02–S03 capacity, and no dependent epic consumes their output before Sprint 05, so the R0 milestone (assessed at the end of Sprint 04) is unaffected.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **US-OBS-001** Metrics pipeline — `/metrics` Prometheus endpoint, the metric catalogue of `20-architecture.md` §12.1 with bounded cardinality and an `env` label, Prometheus scrape config (10 s, 15 d retention).
- **US-OBS-002** Latency-budget instrumentation — per-stage timers (ingest → internal fan-out → client render), the frontend telemetry push endpoint, recording rules expressing the §2 budgets as burn rates.
- **US-OBS-003** Structured logging — `structlog` JSON to stdout, mandatory correlation field set, handler-level redaction filter, runtime per-subsystem log-level override with auto-revert.
- **US-OBS-004** Alerting — Alertmanager with exactly two severities (Page / Ticket) per ADR-0014 §6, grouping/dedup, owner routing, runbook link mandatory per rule.
- **US-OBS-005** Rate-limit budget metrics (`bybit_rate_remaining{endpoint_group}`, `oms_rate_reject_total`) exported here; the SCR-147 UI belongs to E42.
- **US-OBS-007** Support bundle — `POST`-triggered diagnostic bundle with pre-write secret scanning and size cap.
- Health surface: `/health/live`, `/health/ready`, build-info, and `GET /api/v1/admin/health` returning `HealthReport` (`docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`).
- Six provisioned Grafana dashboards as reviewed JSON under `infra/grafana` (`20-architecture.md` §12.4).
- Postgres `system_events` writer feeding `GET /api/v1/admin/incidents` and SCR-144.
- Design, QA and Security tickets for the surfaces above (SCR-143, SCR-144, SCR-152, SCR-156, CMP-178, CMP-210, CMP-207, CMP-092, CMP-076).

## Out of scope
- The Admin screens themselves as finished product UI (SCR-143 system health, SCR-144 incident log) — built in **E42 Admin**; E04 delivers the data contracts, the design specs and the health/incident API.
- Chaos & failure drills as a release gate (**US-OBS-006**) — owned by **E45 Reconciliation, chaos & failover resilience**; E04 only seeds a WS-disconnect harness fixture.
- Loki / centralised log search (deferred by ADR-0014), Tempo/Mimir, any SaaS observability.
- Trading, rule-engine and recorder metrics *implementations* — each owning epic registers its own metrics against the registry E04 provides.
- Android / mobile telemetry (out of scope per owner decision 2026-09-14).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Metrics visible end to end
  Given the api service is running in dev
  When Prometheus scrapes /metrics
  Then every metric named in 20-architecture.md §12.1 that belongs to a module shipped in R0 is present, carries an env label, and the scrape completes in under 50 ms

Scenario: A secret never reaches a log
  Given a Bybit API secret, a session cookie and a TOTP code are passed through log calls, an exception traceback and an httpx request log
  When the JSON log output is captured
  Then none of the three values appears at any log level, and the CI redaction test fails the build if one does

Scenario: Synthetic alert is received (R0 exit criterion 10)
  Given a synthetic condition is injected in staging
  When the rule's for-duration elapses
  Then Alertmanager delivers the alert to the owner's channel within 60 s, the notification names the severity and links to a runbook section in 07-release-and-prr.md

Scenario: Degraded dependency does not fail liveness
  Given QuestDB is stopped
  When /health/live and /health/ready are probed
  Then /health/live returns 200 and /health/ready returns 503 naming questdb, and GET /api/v1/admin/health reports overall=degraded with that component's state and last-good timestamp
```

## Technical notes / design
The observability module (`services/api/candleviewer/observability/`, following the §3 module conventions of `docs/plan/20-architecture.md`) owns a single process-wide Prometheus `CollectorRegistry` plus a `metrics.py` facade so other modules never import `prometheus_client` directly (enforced by an `import-linter` contract from E02). Logging is configured once at process start; the redaction processor is installed at the *handler* level (SR-121) so a new call site cannot bypass it. Correlation ids are carried in a `contextvars.ContextVar` set by the ASGI middleware (`request_id`) and by the WS connection handler (`conn_id`), and copied into every task spawned by OMS/ingestion so async hops do not lose them. Tracing is OpenTelemetry on exactly two paths only (order path, replay session start) — market-data hot loops are metrics-only because sampling them would distort the loop being measured.

## Test plan
Unit: redaction matrix, correlation propagation across `asyncio.create_task`, metric registration idempotence, cardinality guard, health aggregator with each component failing in turn. Contract: `HealthReport` / `Incident` schemas against `22-api-openapi.yaml`; Prometheus exposition format parses with `prometheus_client.parser`. Integration: docker-compose stack with prometheus + grafana + alertmanager; dashboard JSON loads without "panel datasource not found". E2E: synthetic alert drill. Perf: scrape latency under full label set. Coverage ≥85% on the backend observability package.

## Security notes
Threats K1 (key material in logs), U5 (token theft via logs), D3 (over-exposing operational payloads), A-17 (telemetry asset). Controls: SR-006/SR-007 secret wrapper, SR-120…SR-126 logging/redaction/alerting requirements, SR-005 (no secret prefix beyond 4 chars anywhere). `/metrics` binds to the private network only and is never publicly routable. Support bundles are secret-scanned before write, audited, and never uploaded automatically. Data classification: telemetry = Internal; bundles may transit Confidential operational data and stay on the local machine.

## Accessibility notes
E04 ships design specs (not final UI) for SCR-143/SCR-144 and the health chrome components CMP-178, CMP-210, CMP-092, CMP-076, CMP-207. Every health state must be conveyed as a *word* plus a number with units — never colour alone (WCAG 2.2 AA, `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`). Status regions use `role="status"`/`role="alert"` by severity with announcements throttled to ≤1 Hz.

## Performance notes
Instrumentation overhead ≤1% CPU (US-OBS-002 NFR). `/metrics` scrape < 50 ms with the full label set (ADR-0014 validation). Metric cardinality is bounded and documented — symbol/account/env labels only, never order ids or user emails.

## Observability
This epic *is* the observability surface: metrics catalogue §12.1, log field set §12.2, two traced paths §12.3, six dashboards §12.4, two-severity alert policy §12.5, plus `system_events` rows for every operational incident.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All children Done or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition.
- [ ] R0 exit criterion 10 demonstrated live at Sprint Review (dashboards populated, synthetic alert received).
- [ ] ADR-0014 reconciled with what actually shipped; `20-architecture.md` §12 updated if the catalogue diverged.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85% on touched backend packages; CI gate green.
- [ ] STRIDE model for E04 complete and signed off by the Security engineer (E04-X01).
- [ ] QA epic-level regression + exploratory pass recorded (E04-Q01, E04-Q02).
- [ ] Design sign-off (CDO or delegate) on E04-D01/E04-D02 outputs.
- [ ] Runbook entries exist for every alert rule — an alert without a runbook is a merge blocker.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by: E03` — CI/CD pipeline and the dev/staging environments must exist before dashboards, scrape targets and alert routing can be deployed. E02 (monorepo, docker compose with prometheus/grafana) is a transitive prerequisite via E03. E08 (ingestion) and E09 (auth) consume this epic's registry and correlation context but do not block it.

## Branch
`feat/obs-baseline-*`; PRs ≤400 LOC diff, one concern per PR (logging, metrics, health, dashboards, alerting kept separate).

```mermaid
    D01[E04-D01 Design: health & incident specs] --> D02[E04-D02 Design QA + a11y review]
    K01[E04-K01 Spike: tracing & instrumentation overhead] --> T06

```


## Agent guidance

How to pick up work in this epic when multiple agents are running in parallel:

**Dependency order.** Work tickets in `blocked_by` order; a ticket is not pickable until every key in its `blocked_by` list is Done. Design (`-D*`) and spike (`-K*`) tickets generally gate the technical (`-T*`) and story (`-S*`) tickets that consume their output — check each ticket's `blocked_by` field, do not assume numeric order implies dependency order.

**Parallel lanes.** Tickets with disjoint `component` values and no shared `blocked_by` edge can run concurrently: backend (`api`/`data-feeds`) tickets, frontend (`web`) tickets and design (`-D*`) tickets form separate lanes once their own upstream design/contract tickets are Done. QA (`-Q*`) and security (`-X*`) tickets typically depend on the corresponding `-S*`/`-T*` ticket being Done, so they are the last lane per feature slice, not a separate epic-wide phase.

**Shared interfaces to agree first.** Before two agents touch the same contract (API/WS schema, DB table, or statechart) concurrently, the one opening the PR first must land the contract change (OpenAPI/WS schema/migration) and regenerate `packages/protocol`; the second agent rebases on it rather than proposing a second incompatible shape. Statechart JSON under `machines/` is single-owner per PR — check open PRs touching the same `machines/<name>.machine.json` before starting a `statechart`-labelled ticket.

title: Measure instrumentation overhead: metrics, structlog and OTel on the hot paths
body:
## Context
ADR-0014 (`docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0014-observability.md`) asserts that tracing market-data hot loops "would distort the very loop it measures", and US-OBS-002 (`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §28) carries the NFR *measurement overhead ≤1% CPU*. Both are currently assertions, not measurements. Before E04-T03/T06 harden the instrumentation API we need numbers, because retro-fitting a cheaper metrics facade after twenty modules have adopted it is expensive.

Timebox: **3 days**, agreed with the Architect. Not expected to produce production-shippable code; the harness may be promoted into `tests/perf/` if it is clean.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A synthetic hot-loop harness: 20 000 messages/s through a parse → transform → emit pipeline, mirroring the ingestion shape of `20-architecture.md` §12.1 (`ws_messages_total`, `topic_staleness_seconds`, `ingest_queue_depth`).
- Four measured configurations: (a) no instrumentation, (b) Prometheus counters/histograms only, (c) b + structlog JSON at INFO with the redaction processor, (d) c + OpenTelemetry spans at 100% and at 1% sampling.
- Comparison of `prometheus_client` vs a pre-bound-label fast path (label lookup hoisted out of the loop).
- Measurement of `contextvars` propagation cost across `asyncio.create_task` at the same rate.
- Written findings appended to ADR-0014 as an addendum, plus follow-up tickets if any configuration breaches 1% CPU.

## Out of scope
- Choosing the alerting or dashboard stack (already decided in ADR-0014).
- Any real Bybit connection — the harness is synthetic and offline.
- Frontend telemetry overhead (measured in E04-T06 against the real engine).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Overhead quantified per configuration
  Given the harness runs each of the four configurations for 120 s at 20k msg/s
  When results are collected
  Then CPU%, p50/p95/p99 per-message latency and RSS are recorded per configuration with at least 3 repeats and their variance stated

Scenario: Decision criteria applied
  Given configuration (b) exceeds 1% CPU over baseline
  Then the pre-bound-label fast path is adopted as the mandatory pattern in the metrics facade and E04-T03 is updated to enforce it

Scenario: Tracing decision confirmed or overturned
  Given configuration (d) at 100% sampling exceeds 5% CPU over baseline
  Then ADR-0014's "metrics only on market-data hot loops" stands and is recorded as measured rather than assumed; otherwise an addendum records that hot-loop tracing is affordable at the stated sampling rate
```

## Technical notes / design
Run on the reference VPS profile named in `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §3 (4 vCPU / 8 GB), not on the dev workstation, because backend budgets are set against the smaller profile. Measure CPU with `resource.getrusage` deltas plus `psutil` sampling; avoid `time.time()` in the inner loop (use `time.perf_counter_ns` on a sampled 1-in-N basis). Beware of the classic false result: a histogram with a label tuple computed inside the loop is dominated by dict hashing, not by the observation — measure both shapes explicitly.

## Test plan
Not a production ticket; the deliverable is evidence. The harness itself gets a smoke test asserting it produces the expected message count so a broken run is not mistaken for a fast one.

## Security notes
The harness must use synthetic payloads only — no real API keys, no recorded private-WS fixtures. If the redaction processor is exercised, use obviously fake secrets with a distinctive canary prefix.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI surface.

## Performance notes
The whole point: budget is ≤1% CPU for instrumentation (US-OBS-002 NFR) and the backend-internal latency envelope is ≤20 ms p95 (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` budget #6) — instrumentation must not consume a measurable slice of that.

## Observability
N/A — this spike measures observability rather than adding it.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Numbers recorded in the ticket with hardware profile, repeat count and variance.
- [ ] ADR-0014 addendum merged (even if the outcome is "no change").
- [ ] Follow-up tickets filed for whichever path is chosen, linking these findings.
- [ ] Findings presented at Sprint Review.
- [ ] `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` updated if a new risk surfaced.
- [ ] Harness branch promoted to `tests/perf/` or explicitly marked throwaway.

## Dependencies
`E03` — needs a runnable containerised environment and a CI runner profile to measure against.

## Branch
`spike/obs-baseline-overhead`; findings PR is docs-only, harness PR separate if promoted.

## References
- `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0014-observability.md`
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-OBS-002
- `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §2, §3, §5.1
- `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §12.1


## Agent execution brief

**Read first**
1. `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0014-observability.md`
2. `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-OBS-002
3. `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §2, §3, §5.1
4. `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §12.1

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- `infra/`
- `.github/workflows/`
- `tests/` — mirrored unit/integration test paths for the module(s) above

**Interfaces you must not break**
- None beyond what's listed in References.

**Commands**
- `pnpm lint`
- `pnpm verify`

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `spike/obs-baseline-overhead`
- PR title: "E04-K01: Measure instrumentation overhead: metrics, structlog and OTel on the hot paths"
- PR description includes: `Closes #<issue>`
- Required reviewers (CODEOWNERS): @CandleViewer/devsecops
- Labels: type/spike, area/infra-devops, priority/p1-high, perf

**Done means**
- Numbers recorded in the ticket with hardware profile, repeat count and variance.
- ADR-0014 addendum merged (even if the outcome is "no change").
- Follow-up tickets filed for whichever path is chosen, linking these findings.
- Findings presented at Sprint Review.
- `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` updated if a new risk surfaced.
- Harness branch promoted to `tests/perf/` or explicitly marked throwaway.

**Do NOT**
- Choosing the alerting or dashboard stack (already decided in ADR-0014).
- Any real Bybit connection — the harness is synthetic and offline.
- Frontend telemetry overhead (measured in E04-T06 against the real engine).

**If blocked**
- Comment on this ticket's GitHub issue naming the exact blocking condition (missing contract, failing upstream gate, ambiguous acceptance criterion) and the ticket key it depends on. Move the issue's Status to **Blocked**. Do not silently work around a failing gate, widen scope, or guess at an undocumented contract — stop and wait for the blocker to clear.

## Agent-delivery adaptations (owner decision 2026-09-25)
Delivery is executed by parallel AI agents with a single human owner (`@basiltt`). Where this ticket's text assumes the original 15-person org, apply these substitutions — they are binding and satisfy the corresponding DoR/DoD items:
- **Architect / CDO / Security-engineer sign-off or countersignature** → the **owner's** `approved` comment on this issue, or owner merge of the PR. No other human role exists. Do not block on a missing countersignature — proceed and record "owner approval pending" in the PR.
- **Design tooling**: *Figma* → **Penpot** (`docs/design/README.md`); frames on a page named after this ticket; exports via `docs/design/_tools/penpot_export.py`. Bind only to semantic tokens in `packages/ui/tokens/`.
- **Moderated usability / participant sessions** → a documented **heuristic evaluation** (Nielsen + the trading-specific heuristics in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`), a written session protocol ready for the owner to run later, and an **owner walkthrough** checklist posted on the issue. Never fabricate participants, timings or quotes; label all findings `(heuristic)`.
- **CVD / contrast validation** → computed programmatically (WCAG contrast matrix over the token JSON; CVD simulation via a documented script), attached as artefacts.
- **Spikes**: findings go to `docs/plan/spikes/<KEY>.md` via a normal PR (branch `spike/<epic>-<slug>`); any ADR named by the spike uses the **next free number** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` (ADR-0001…0016 are taken).
- **Dependencies**: `blocked_by` now lists the concrete prerequisite tickets (not whole epics). Start when those are **merged** (In Test or Done).
- Anything that genuinely needs a human that is not the owner (external pen-test vendor, legal) stays as-is and is flagged `needs-owner` on the issue.

title: Implement structlog JSON logging with handler-level redaction filter
body:
## Context
Implements the redaction and field-shape half of **US-OBS-003** (`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §28). `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §12.2 fixes the log format; `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §6.9 makes it mandatory: SR-120 (structured JSON, fixed field set, no free-form interpolation of user/exchange data), SR-121 (redaction installed at handler level so a new call site cannot bypass it, covering tracebacks, HTTP-client logging and third-party loggers), SR-122 (tokens/cookies/signatures/TOTP never logged at any level), SR-123 (body logging off by default), SR-124 (restrictive permissions, rotation, excluded from CI artefact upload). Threat K1 in §5 rates "key secret written to application logs" as **High**.

This is the first ticket of the epic because every other module's logging inherits from it — if it lands late, call sites ship with ad hoc `logging.getLogger()` usage that then has to be unpicked.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `services/api/src/cv/obs/logging.py`: a single `configure_logging(env, level)` entry point called exactly once at process start (FastAPI lifespan and every worker entrypoint: ingestion, recorder, replay).
- structlog processor chain producing JSON to stdout with the mandatory fields of `20-architecture.md` §12.2: `ts`, `level`, `logger`, `event`, `env`, `request_id`/`conn_id`, `user_id`, `account_id`, `symbol`, `order_link_id`, `trade_group_id`, `latency_ms`. Absent values are omitted, never emitted as the string `"None"`.
- `RedactionProcessor` installed as a `logging.Filter` on the root handler (not as a structlog-only processor), so stdlib loggers from `httpx`, `websockets`, `sqlalchemy` and `pybit` are covered.
- Redaction rules: exact key names (`api_key`, `api_secret`, `secret`, `password`, `cookie`, `set-cookie`, `authorization`, `x-bapi-sign`, `x-bapi-api-key`, `totp`, `recovery_code`, `session`, `csrf`) redacted by key; value-shape patterns (Bybit key/secret charsets, JWT-like `xx.yy.zz`, 6-digit TOTP adjacent to a totp-ish key) redacted by value; replacement is `"[redacted:<reason>]"` so the loss is visible rather than silent.
- Traceback scrubbing: exception `args` and locals rendered through the same filter.
- A `Secret[str]` wrapper type (SR-007) whose `__str__`/`__repr__`/`__format__` return `[redacted]`, used by the key store — defence in depth alongside the filter.
- Log rotation + `0600` permissions configured in the compose logging driver; `.gitignore` and CI artefact-upload exclusion for `*.log` (SR-124).
- Request/response body logging behind an off-by-default, time-boxed flag (SR-123) that logs its own activation as an audit event.

## Out of scope
- Correlation-id *propagation* and the runtime log-level override — **E04-T02**.
- Shipping logs anywhere (Loki is deliberately deferred by ADR-0014); stdout + compose driver only.
- Frontend logging.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Canary secrets never reach the output
  Given a Bybit api_secret, a session cookie, an X-BAPI-SIGN header value and a 6-digit TOTP code, each containing a unique canary string
  When they are logged at DEBUG via structlog, via a stdlib logger, inside an exception traceback, and via an httpx request log
  Then no canary string appears anywhere in captured stdout, and each site shows [redacted:<reason>] instead

Scenario: A new call site cannot bypass redaction
  Given a module obtains a logger with logging.getLogger(__name__) and never touches structlog
  When it logs a dict containing api_secret
  Then the value is still redacted, because the filter lives on the handler

Scenario: Field shape is stable
  When any log line is emitted
  Then it parses as a single JSON object, ts is RFC 3339 UTC, level is one of debug|info|warning|error|critical, env is present, and absent correlation fields are omitted rather than rendered as the string None

Scenario: Body logging is off by default
  Given no troubleshooting flag is set
  When a request with a JSON body is handled
  Then neither the request nor the response body is logged; enabling the flag writes an audit event and the flag auto-expires after its time box
```

## Technical notes / design
Processor order matters: `merge_contextvars` → `add_log_level` → `add_timestamp(utc, iso)` → `StackInfoRenderer` → `format_exc_info` → **redaction** → `JSONRenderer(serializer=orjson.dumps)`. Redaction must sit *after* `format_exc_info` or the traceback string is already assembled unredacted. Bridge stdlib logging via `structlog.stdlib.ProcessorFormatter` **and** additionally attach the redaction `logging.Filter` to the root handler — belt and braces, because the ProcessorFormatter path is only taken for records that reach that handler.

Cost control: the key-name check is a frozenset membership test; the value-pattern scan is a single pre-compiled alternation and is applied only to `str` values under a length cap (values > 4 KiB are truncated with a marker before scanning, so one huge payload cannot stall the loop). Depth-limit recursion into nested dicts/lists to 6 levels and mark deeper structures `[redacted:depth]` rather than recursing unboundedly on a cyclic structure.

Error codes: none introduced. Config keys: `CV_LOG_LEVEL` (default `INFO`), `CV_LOG_FORMAT` (`json`|`console`, `console` only permitted when `CV_ENV=dev`), `CV_LOG_BODIES_UNTIL` (RFC 3339 instant, absent = off).

## Test plan
- Unit: redaction matrix (≥20 cases) covering key-name hits, value-shape hits, nested dicts, lists of dicts, tracebacks, third-party logger records, oversize values, cyclic structures. Field-shape golden test. `Secret[str]` repr/str/format test. Console-format refusal outside dev.
- Unit (regression guard): a test that walks the installed handlers and asserts the redaction filter is attached — so a future refactor that drops it fails CI.
- Integration: run the api under uvicorn, issue a request with an `Authorization` header and a body, capture stdout, assert no header value appears.
- CI gate: the canary test is wired as a required check (SR-121 verification method: unit, integration).
- Coverage target ≥85% on `cv/obs`.

## Security notes
Directly implements SR-120…SR-124 and mitigates threat K1 (High) and U5. Data classification: logs are Internal but may transit Confidential order data — hence the field allow-list. Requires the `security` label and a Security-engineer review comment before Done (DoD §8 cross-kind gating). Note the failure mode to review for: redaction that raises an exception inside the logging path must never crash the caller — the filter wraps its own body in a try/except that, on failure, drops the *record* rather than emitting it unredacted.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI surface.

## Performance notes
Per-record redaction overhead must stay within the envelope measured in E04-K01; target ≤5 µs for a typical 10-field record. Logging must be non-blocking with respect to the event loop: stdout writes go through a `QueueHandler`/`QueueListener` pair so a slow pipe reader cannot stall the ingestion loop.

Adds `log_records_total{level}` and `log_redactions_total{reason}` counters — a sudden spike in `log_redactions_total` is itself a signal that a new call site is trying to log secrets.

title: Propagate correlation ids across HTTP, WS and async tasks; runtime log-level override
body:
## Context
Completes **US-OBS-003** (`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §28): *"Given a user submits an order, then every log line for that action shares a correlation id spanning API, OMS, exchange adapter and WS notification"* and *"When I raise the log level for one subsystem at runtime, then only that subsystem becomes verbose and the change reverts automatically after a timeout"*. Without propagation the JSON logs from E04-T01 are well-formatted but uncorrelated, which is exactly the failure mode ADR-0014 accepts when it defers Loki: grep-over-files only works if the correlation fields are reliably present.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `cv/obs/context.py`: `contextvars` for `request_id`, `conn_id`, `user_id`, `account_id`, `symbol`, `order_link_id`, `trade_group_id`, with a `bind_context(**fields)` context manager.
- ASGI middleware that accepts an inbound `X-Correlation-Id` (validated as a UUIDv4; rejected and replaced if malformed — an attacker must not be able to inject arbitrary strings into the log field set) or mints one, binds it, and echoes it on the response.
- WS gateway hook binding `conn_id` at `auth_ok` and `request_id` per inbound frame, per `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` (the `system` topic is auto-subscribed at `auth_ok`, so the connection is identified from that moment).
- `cv.obs.spawn(coro, name=...)`: a `create_task` wrapper that copies the current context, plus a lint rule (Semgrep) banning bare `asyncio.create_task` in application modules so a hop cannot silently drop correlation.
- Correlation id carried into the OMS `order_link_id` log field and onto outbound exchange requests where the adapter supports a client-supplied reference, so an exchange-side reject can be traced back.
- Runtime log-level override: `PUT /api/v1/admin/log-level` with body `{subsystem, level, ttl_seconds}` (max ttl 3600, default 900), RBAC `admin:write`, audited as `settings.change`; a background task restores the previous level on expiry and on process restart the override is simply absent (it is deliberately not persisted).
- `system_events` row written when an override is set or expires (`component='api'`, `kind='log_level_override'`).

## Out of scope
- OpenTelemetry spans (E04-T06 covers the traced order path).
- Persisting overrides across restarts — deliberately not done; a forgotten DEBUG level on a hot path is a performance hazard.
- Frontend correlation display.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: One id spans the whole order path
  Given a client submits an order over HTTP with no X-Correlation-Id header
  When the request flows through api, oms.validate, the Bybit adapter and the resulting private-WS notification
  Then every log line emitted on that path carries the same request_id, and the value is returned to the client in the X-Correlation-Id response header

Scenario: Async hop does not lose context
  Given a handler spawns background work with cv.obs.spawn
  When that work logs
  Then the log line carries the originating request_id, user_id and account_id

Scenario: A malformed inbound correlation id is rejected
  Given a request arrives with X-Correlation-Id: "'; DROP TABLE" or a 10 KB string
  Then the value is discarded, a fresh UUIDv4 is minted, and the rejected value is not written into any log field

Scenario: Runtime override is scoped and self-reverting
  Given the ingestion subsystem's level is raised to DEBUG with ttl_seconds=60
  Then only loggers under the ingestion namespace emit DEBUG, the change is audited, and after 60 s the previous level is restored automatically without a restart

Scenario: Override requires privilege
  Given a Viewer calls PUT /api/v1/admin/log-level
  Then the response is 403, no level changes, and an audit row records the denied attempt
```

## Technical notes / design
`contextvars` propagate automatically into `await`ed coroutines but a task created with `asyncio.create_task` inherits a *copy* at creation time — which is what we want — while `loop.run_in_executor` and thread pools do **not**, so the wrapper must explicitly `contextvars.copy_context().run(...)` for thread offloads (relevant for the QuestDB ILP writer and any blocking DB call). This is the single most common way correlation silently breaks; the Semgrep rule and a dedicated unit test both target it.

The log-level override applies to the *logger namespace* (`cv.ingestion`, `cv.oms`, `cv.rules`, `cv.recorder`, `cv.api`, `cv.ws`), enumerated as a closed set in the request schema so an operator cannot set DEBUG on the root logger and flood the disk. TTL enforcement uses a monotonic deadline checked by a 5-second ticker, not a one-shot timer, so a suspended process still reverts on resume.

## Test plan
- Unit: context binding/unbinding; `spawn` inheritance; executor offload inheritance; malformed header rejection (fuzz a set of hostile values); namespace-scoped level application; TTL expiry with a fake clock; closed-set validation rejecting `root` and `""`.
- Contract: `PUT /api/v1/admin/log-level` request/response schema added to `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` and diff-checked in CI.
- Integration: end-to-end request through api → a stubbed OMS → a stubbed adapter, asserting a single id across all captured lines.
- E2E: a WS connection's `conn_id` appears on frames logged for that connection.
- Coverage ≥85%.

## Security notes
Inbound correlation ids are untrusted input written into a structured log field — validate strictly (UUIDv4 regex, length cap) to prevent log injection/forging of another request's id. The override endpoint is an admin surface: RBAC `admin:write`, audited (`settings.change` is in the mandatory audited-action list in `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.10.1), capped TTL, closed namespace set, and it must never be able to enable body logging (that stays behind `CV_LOG_BODIES_UNTIL` from E04-T01 with its own authorisation).

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI surface in this ticket (the admin control lives in E42).

## Performance notes
`contextvars` get/set is nanosecond-scale; the risk is the volume increase from a DEBUG override, hence the TTL cap and namespace scoping. Verify under E04-K01's harness that binding 7 context vars per message does not breach the ≤1% CPU instrumentation budget.

## Observability
Adds `log_level_overrides_active` gauge and a `system_events` row per override set/expire so an operator can see from SCR-144 that the system was deliberately verbose during an incident window.

title: Build the Prometheus registry, metrics facade and R0 metric catalogue
body:
## Context
Implements **US-OBS-001** (`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §28): every subsystem exports structured metrics, labelled by symbol/account/environment, with no secret or personal data, and with a local fallback log entry when the scrape path fails so no gap is invisible. The authoritative catalogue is `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §12.1; ADR-0014 makes metrics part of the DoD of every module, which means this facade is a platform contract consumed by E08 (ingestion), E09 (auth), E16 (recorder), E29 (OMS) and E35 (rules) — its ergonomics matter more than its internals.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `cv/obs/metrics.py`: a single process-wide `CollectorRegistry`, a `Metrics` facade exposing `counter/gauge/histogram/enum` factories, and a module-registration helper. Other modules import *this*, never `prometheus_client` directly — enforced by an `import-linter` contract (E02) so the rule is mechanical rather than cultural.
- Every metric in `20-architecture.md` §12.1 declared in a single catalogue module with name, type, unit, labels, help text and the alert it feeds — declared here even when the owning module ships later, so the dashboard and alert JSON can be written against real names instead of guesses. Modules not yet built register no samples; the catalogue records them as `planned` and a test asserts that every `planned` entry has an owning epic.
- R0-live metrics implemented end to end: `event_loop_lag_seconds`, `ws_connection_state{socket}`, `ws_messages_total{topic}`, `ws_message_bytes_total`, `topic_staleness_seconds{topic}`, `ingest_queue_depth{stage}`, `book_resync_total{symbol,reason}`, `engine_process_seconds{engine}`, `pg_pool_in_use`, `pg_query_seconds`, `questdb_write_seconds`, plus the process/GC collectors.
- `bybit_rate_remaining{endpoint_group}` and `oms_rate_reject_total` exported from the adapter's rate-limit accounting — the metric half of **US-OBS-005** (the SCR-147 screen is E42's).
- Mandatory `env` label injected by the registry itself (not by each call site) so demo and live can never blur together.
- **Cardinality guard**: a registered metric declares `max_series`; a background check samples the registry every 60 s and, on breach, logs an error, increments `metric_cardinality_breach_total{metric}` and stops accepting *new* label values for that metric rather than letting the registry grow unbounded.
- `GET /metrics` on a private-bind-only listener, plus Prometheus scrape config (10 s interval, 15 d retention) and the compose wiring in `infra/prometheus/`.
- Scrape-failure fallback: an internal ticker writes a compact metrics snapshot to the structured log every 5 min, so a Prometheus outage still leaves a trail (US-OBS-001 third scenario).
- `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §12.1 updated with any name/label corrections found during implementation.

## Out of scope
- Dashboards (E04-S01), alert rules (E04-T05), latency budget recording rules and frontend telemetry (E04-T06).
- Metrics whose owning subsystem does not exist yet — declared as `planned`, implemented by the owning epic.
- `engine_metrics` QuestDB writes (`21-database-schema.md` §4.13) — that join-to-market-data path is E16 Recorder's.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Catalogue is complete and exposition parses
  Given the api process is running
  When GET /metrics is scraped
  Then the payload parses with the Prometheus text parser, and every metric in 20-architecture.md §12.1 marked live-in-R0 is present with an env label, a HELP line and a unit-suffixed name

Scenario: No secret or personal data in labels
  Given the full catalogue is registered and exercised
  When label names and values are enumerated
  Then no label is an api key, session token, email, user name, order id or free-form exchange message, and a CI test fails the build if a disallowed label name is introduced

Scenario: Cardinality is bounded
  Given a metric declares max_series=200 and 250 distinct label combinations are produced
  Then series 201+ are not created, metric_cardinality_breach_total increments, an error is logged naming the metric, and the process does not crash or leak memory

Scenario: Scrape failure leaves a trail
  Given Prometheus cannot reach the endpoint for 10 minutes
  Then at least two fallback snapshot log entries have been written with the key gauges, so the outage window is not silently empty

Scenario: Endpoint is not publicly reachable
  Given the service is deployed per the compose topology
  When /metrics is requested from outside the private network
  Then the connection is refused, and a test asserts the listener binds to the private interface only
```

## Technical notes / design
Label tuples are pre-bound at registration where the label values are known at startup (per-topic, per-stage, per-socket) — E04-K01 measures whether in-loop `labels()` lookup is affordable; if not, the facade's API only exposes the pre-bound form on hot paths. Histograms use explicit buckets tuned to the budgets in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` (e.g. `event_loop_lag_seconds` buckets around the 50 ms p99 target and the 100 ms alert threshold; `ws_fanout_latency_seconds` around the 20 ms p99 budget) — default buckets would put both thresholds inside one bucket and make the alert unprovable.

`event_loop_lag_seconds` is measured by a task that sleeps a known interval and records the overshoot; run it at 100 ms cadence, not 1 s, or a 100 ms lag alert is measuring its own sampling error.

A gauge like `topic_staleness_seconds` must be computed *at scrape time* from the last-update timestamp (a `Gauge` with a callback), not pushed on update — otherwise a topic that stops updating freezes its staleness at the last pushed value, which is precisely the failure this metric exists to catch. This inversion is the single most important detail in the ticket.

Config keys: `CV_METRICS_ENABLED` (default true), `CV_METRICS_BIND` (default `127.0.0.1:9108`), `CV_ENV` (`dev|staging|demo|live`).

## Test plan
- Unit: facade factories, duplicate-registration idempotence, `env` label injection, cardinality guard (breach, recovery, no-leak), staleness callback returns a growing value when updates stop, histogram bucket edges match the documented budgets, disallowed-label-name guard.
- Contract: exposition output parsed by `prometheus_client.parser.text_string_to_metric_families`; a golden catalogue snapshot test fails on an unreviewed metric name/label change (metric names are a contract with dashboards and alerts).
- Integration: compose stack — Prometheus target shows `up=1`, a query for each live metric returns samples.
- Perf: scrape latency < 50 ms with the full label set at max declared cardinality (ADR-0014 validation clause).
- Chaos: kill Prometheus, assert fallback log entries appear.
- Coverage ≥85%.

## Security notes
SR-125 requires security-relevant metrics to be exported and alerted on — failed logins, lockouts, step-up failures, permission-check failures, credential-verification failures, rate-limit rejections, rule circuit-breaker trips, audit-chain verification failures, egress IP changes, clock drift, disk high-watermark, WS desync rate. Declare all of these in the catalogue now (as `planned` where the owner epic is later) so E09/E27/E35 have names to implement against. `/metrics` is unauthenticated by convention but must bind privately only (`20-architecture.md` §13.1: loopback/WSL-internal binds, no public ingress) — an exposed `/metrics` leaks order rates, account count and trading activity. Label values are a disclosure surface: never an email, never an order id, never an exchange error string.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI surface.

## Performance notes
Scrape < 50 ms at full cardinality; instrumentation overhead within the E04-K01 envelope (≤1% CPU). Bounded cardinality is itself a performance control: symbol ≤ 10, account ≤ 5, env = 1 per process, per the fixed small-scale target in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §1.4.

## Observability
Self-observability: `metric_cardinality_breach_total{metric}`, `metrics_scrape_duration_seconds`, `metrics_registry_series` gauge.

title: Implement health, readiness, build-info and the aggregated admin health report
body:
## Context
ADR-0014 §7 requires `/healthz` (liveness) and `/readyz` (readiness including migrations-at-head and storage reachability) plus an aggregated module health report that backs the Admin health console — *"the operator's first stop"*. The contract already exists in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`: `GET /health/live`, `GET /health/ready` and `GET /admin/health` returning `HealthReport` (overall, version, git_sha, uptime_seconds, server_time, clock_offset_ms, components[], alerts_active). SCR-143 (`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` §"Admin: system health") consumes it and states a hard requirement: *"the page works when the backend is partially down"* and *"all tiles resolve independently, no tile can block another"*.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `GET /health/live` — process-only liveness, never touches the database, `security: []`, sub-millisecond.
- `GET /health/ready` — 200 only when Alembic is at a single head, Postgres is reachable, QuestDB is reachable and the configured exchange adapter has completed its first instruments-info load; 503 with a body naming the unready components otherwise.
- `GET /api/v1/admin/health` — `HealthReport` per the OpenAPI schema, `x-rbac: {permissions: [admin:read]}`, aggregating probes for: `postgres`, `questdb`, `parquet_store`, `bybit_public_ws`, `bybit_private_ws`, `bybit_rest`, `oms`, `rule_engine`, `recorder`, `disk`.
- A `HealthProbe` protocol (`name`, `timeout`, `async check() -> ComponentHealth{state, latency_ms, detail, last_good_at}`) with a registry so each module contributes its own probe; modules not yet built register a `not_deployed` probe rather than being silently absent.
- Probes run **concurrently with per-probe timeouts** and independent failure isolation; `overall` is the worst component state (`healthy` > `degraded` > `warning` > `down` ordering defined explicitly).
- Build-info: version, git sha, build time, env — exposed on the health report and consumed by **CMP-207 BuildFooter** (SCR-119 Help & about); surfaced as a `build_info{version,commit,env}` Prometheus gauge of constant value 1 so dashboards can annotate deploys.
- Health snapshot published to the WS `system` topic (`docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §`system`, 1000 ms cadence, auto-subscribed) — the `health` and `exchange` fields of `SystemUpdate`.
- `system_events` rows (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.10.2) written on every component state transition, with `component`, `kind`, `severity`, `message`, `details`, `correlation_id` — this is the data behind `GET /admin/incidents` and SCR-144.

## Out of scope
- SCR-143 / SCR-144 as built UI (E42 Admin) — design specs only here (E04-D01).
- `GET /admin/incidents` grouping/read-model beyond writing the underlying rows — E42.
- Backups health (`backups` table) — E48/admin scope.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Liveness is independent of dependencies
  Given Postgres and QuestDB are both stopped
  When GET /health/live is probed
  Then it returns 200 within 50 ms and has issued zero database queries

Scenario: Readiness blocks on migrations
  Given the database has two Alembic heads or is behind the code's head revision
  When GET /health/ready is probed
  Then it returns 503 and the body names the migration state as the blocking reason

Scenario: One slow probe does not block the report
  Given the parquet_store probe hangs for 30 s
  When GET /api/v1/admin/health is requested
  Then the response returns within 2 s, parquet_store is reported as degraded with reason "probe timeout", every other component reports normally, and overall is degraded

Scenario: State transitions are recorded
  Given bybit_public_ws transitions healthy -> down -> healthy
  Then two system_events rows are written with component='exchange' (or 'ws'), the correct severity and a human-readable message, and both appear in GET /api/v1/admin/incidents

Scenario: RBAC on the detailed report
  Given a Viewer requests GET /api/v1/admin/health
  Then the response is 403 and no component detail is disclosed
```

## Technical notes / design
Probe results are **cached with a short TTL (2 s) and served from cache**, with refresh happening on a background ticker rather than on request. Without this, SCR-143 polling at 1 Hz from three sessions triples the probe load on a system that is, by hypothesis, already degraded — the screen that diagnoses the outage must not deepen it. The ticker also means the report is available instantly even when a probe is timing out, satisfying the "page works when the backend is partially down" requirement.

`clock_offset_ms` comes from the exchange time sync (US-MKT-009's responsibility in E08); until E08 lands, the probe reports `not_deployed` rather than a fake zero — a fabricated healthy value is worse than an honest gap, because `bybit_clock_drift_ms > 1500` is an alerting condition.

`last_good_at` per component is mandatory: SCR-143's degraded state requires "per-subsystem amber with the reason and the last good timestamp".

State ordering for `overall`: `down` > `warning` > `degraded` > `healthy` — define once in an enum with an explicit severity rank and test it, because "worst of" logic implemented ad hoc per caller is a classic source of a green dashboard over a broken system.

## Test plan
- Unit: worst-of aggregation across every state combination; per-probe timeout isolation; cache TTL behaviour; `not_deployed` handling; state-transition detection producing exactly one `system_events` row per transition (not one per poll — test the edge-trigger explicitly).
- Contract: responses validated against `HealthReport`, `Incident` and the liveness/readiness schemas in `22-api-openapi.yaml`; CI contract diff gate.
- Integration: compose stack with each dependency stopped in turn, asserting the documented status codes and report shapes.
- E2E: WS `system` snapshot contains the health block within 1 s of connect.
- Chaos: stop Postgres mid-report; assert no unhandled exception and a correct 503 from readiness.
- Coverage ≥85%.

## Security notes
`/health/live` and `/health/ready` are unauthenticated (needed by the container orchestrator) and must therefore disclose **nothing** beyond a coarse state — no versions, no hostnames, no component detail, no stack traces. The detailed `/admin/health` is `admin:read` gated. `detail` strings must never include connection strings, credentials or raw exchange error payloads — they are rendered into an operator UI and pass through logs. Relevant threat: D3 (information disclosure to an under-privileged viewer).

## Accessibility notes
No UI in this ticket, but the API shape is an a11y constraint: every component state is returned as a machine-readable **word** plus a numeric value with an explicit unit, so SCR-143 can satisfy "each tile shows a number with units plus a state word, never colour alone" without inventing text client-side.

## Performance notes
SCR-143 budget: health tiles subscribe at 1 Hz and the page must stay under 2 ms scripting per frame — served from the 2 s cache, the endpoint must respond p95 < 100 ms even while degraded. `/health/live` p99 < 10 ms.

## Observability
`build_info{version,commit,env}` gauge; `health_component_state{component}` gauge (0 healthy … 3 down) so alerts can be written against components directly; `health_probe_duration_seconds{component}` histogram; `system_events` rows per transition.

- [ ] Security review of the unauthenticated probe responses (no detail leakage).
- [ ] Demo: dependency stopped live, report shows degraded with last-good timestamp.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue.

title: Configure Alertmanager: two-severity rule set, routing, grouping and runbook links
body:
## Context
Implements **US-OBS-004** (`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §28): critical conditions raise alerts; critical alerts deliver through every configured channel and bypass mute and quiet hours; repeated identical alerts are grouped with an occurrence count rather than repeated verbatim. NFR: *alert rules are defined as configuration and version-controlled, not hard-coded*. The policy is fixed by ADR-0014 §6 and `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §12.5 — exactly **two severities**, because, as ADR-0014 puts it, with one operator *"a noisy alert set will be muted, and then the real one will be missed"*. This is R0 exit criterion 10: *a synthetic alert fires and is received*.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `infra/prometheus/rules/*.yml` — version-controlled alerting rules, two severities only:
  - **Page**: `naked_position_alerts_total > 0`; `oms_unknown_orders > 0` for 60 s; Postgres down; clock drift blocking trading (`bybit_clock_drift_ms > 1500`); `disk_used_ratio > 0.95`.
  - **Ticket**: public WS down > 60 s; high `book_resync_total` rate (> 5/min); `event_loop_lag_seconds` p99 > 100 ms for 5 min; `disk_used_ratio > 0.8`; `rule_autodisarm_total` increase; demo/live mismatch attempts; certificate/credential expiry approaching.
- Security alerts from SR-125: failed-login/lockout spikes, permission-check failures, credential-verification failures, rate-limit rejections, audit-chain verification failure, egress IP change. Rules are authored now against the catalogue names declared in E04-T03 even where the emitting module lands later; a rule whose metric is absent must be `absent()`-guarded so it does not sit permanently pending and unnoticed.
- `infra/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml` — routing tree, grouping (`group_by: [alertname, component, env]`, `group_wait 30s`, `group_interval 5m`, `repeat_interval 4h` for Ticket / `30m` for Page), inhibition rules (a Page for a dependency suppresses dependent Tickets), and a `mute_time_intervals` quiet-hours window that **Page severity bypasses**, and that an SR-125 security Ticket (a rule labelled `quiet_hours: bypass`, #2621) bypasses too: it goes to the ticket channel at once, day or night, and is not a page. A general Ticket is sent at the window's end only if it is still firing: one that fires and resolves inside the window is never sent.
- Owner routing out-of-band per SR-126: a channel that does not depend on the app being healthy (e.g. a push/webhook provider reachable independently of the api container), with Page and Ticket visibly distinguishable in the notification itself.
- Every rule carries `annotations.runbook_url` pointing at a section of `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md`; **a CI check fails the build if any rule lacks a runbook link or a valid anchor** — ADR-0014: *"An alert without a runbook is not allowed to be created."*
- A `SyntheticAlert` test condition and a `make alert-drill` target that fires it end to end.
- Promtool unit tests (`promtool test rules`) for every rule, using synthetic series that cross the threshold and then recover.

## Out of scope
- User-facing trading alerts (price/indicator alerts) — E40 Alerts; this ticket is system alerting only.
- The in-app notification centre (SCR-014) and disconnected state (SCR-152) UI — E10/E42; E04-D01 provides the health-state design spec.
- Chaos drills as a release gate — E45 (US-OBS-006).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Synthetic alert reaches the owner (R0 exit criterion 10)
  Given the synthetic Page condition is injected in staging
  When the rule's for-duration elapses
  Then the notification is received on the owner's out-of-band channel within 60 s, is labelled Page, names the component, and contains a working runbook link

Scenario: Quiet hours never swallow a Page
  Given a mute time interval is active
  When a Page-severity alert fires
  Then it is delivered anyway, while a Ticket-severity alert fired in the same window is delivered when the interval ends only if it is still firing (one that resolves inside it is never sent), except an SR-125 security Ticket (`quiet_hours: bypass`), which is never muted: it goes to the ticket channel at once and is not a page

Scenario: Repetition is grouped, not repeated
  Given the same alert fires 50 times in 10 minutes
  Then the owner receives one grouped notification carrying an occurrence count, not 50 messages

Scenario: Every rule has a runbook
  Given a new alerting rule is added without an annotations.runbook_url
  When CI runs
  Then the build fails naming the offending rule

Scenario: A rule over a not-yet-emitted metric is visible, not silent
  Given a rule references a metric no running module emits
  Then the absent() guard raises a Ticket-severity "expected metric missing" alert rather than the rule sitting silently pending forever

Scenario: Dependency inhibition
  Given Postgres is down (Page)
  Then dependent Ticket alerts caused by that outage are inhibited and do not add noise
```

## Technical notes / design
Use recording rules for anything a human would otherwise read as a raw number — `20-architecture.md` §12.5 conditions are expressed over the burn-rate recording rules delivered in E04-T06 where an SLO exists. `for:` durations matter more than thresholds here: a 60 s `for` on `oms_unknown_orders` is the difference between catching a genuinely stuck order and paging on a normal in-flight moment.

The most common failure in this configuration is not a missing rule but a **rule that can never fire** — a typo'd metric name, a label matcher that matches nothing, or a `for:` longer than the condition ever persists. Hence: promtool unit tests per rule (mandatory, not optional) and `absent()` guards. A rule that has never fired in staging by the R0 PRR is treated as unproven, not as "no problems found".

Config keys: `CV_ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL` (secret, injected at process start, never in the repo), `CV_ALERT_QUIET_HOURS`, `CV_ENV`.

## Test plan
- Unit: `promtool test rules` per rule file — series that cross the threshold, series that stay just under, and recovery; assert `for` durations.
- Config: `amtool check-config` in CI; routing-tree simulation (`amtool config routes test`) asserting Page and Ticket land on their intended receivers.
- CI gate: runbook-link presence and anchor validity.
- Integration: compose stack — inject a synthetic condition, assert the webhook receiver (a test double) receives the payload with the expected labels.
- E2E drill: staging, real channel, owner confirms receipt; recorded on the ticket as R0 exit evidence.
- Chaos: Alertmanager restarted mid-firing; assert the alert re-delivers rather than being lost.

## Security notes
SR-126: alert routing must reach the Owner out-of-band, on a channel that does not depend on the app being healthy, with P1 distinguishable from informational. The webhook URL/token is a secret — injected from the host keychain path described in `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` SR-002, never committed, and covered by gitleaks. Alert payloads are an information-disclosure surface (they leave the box): they must carry component, severity, threshold and runbook link — never account ids, order ids, key material or raw exchange payloads. Include SR-125's security-relevant conditions in the rule set. Alertmanager's own UI binds privately only.

## Accessibility notes
Notification content must be readable as plain text without colour or emoji carrying meaning alone — severity is always the word "Page" or "Ticket" (`05-accessibility-standard.md` non-colour-redundancy principle applied to notifications).

## Performance notes
Rule evaluation interval 30 s; total evaluation time must stay well under the interval (assert via `prometheus_rule_group_last_duration_seconds`). Alert delivery latency target: condition true → notification received ≤ 60 s for Page.

## Observability
`ALERTS` / `ALERTS_FOR_STATE` are scraped; add a meta-alert on `alertmanager_notifications_failed_total > 0` — the alerting system's own failure must itself be alerted, or the whole edifice fails silently. Watchdog/deadman's-switch alert always firing, so a *lack* of the watchdog notification indicates the pipeline is dead.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios verified; promtool tests green in CI.
- [ ] Every rule has a runbook section in `07-release-and-prr.md`; CI link check green.
- [ ] Synthetic alert drill executed in staging with owner confirmation recorded (R0 exit criterion 10 evidence).
- [ ] Watchdog and `notifications_failed` meta-alerts in place.
- [ ] Security engineer review of payload content and secret handling.
- [ ] Demo at Sprint Review: fire and receive.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue.

`E04-T03` (metric names to alert on), `E04-T04` (component health states). Runbook sections are authored in `E04-T07`, which in turn depends on this rule set — the two are co-developed and land in the same sprint, with T07 as the closing ticket.

title: Instrument the latency budget end to end and add the frontend telemetry endpoint
body:
## Context
Implements **US-OBS-002** (`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §28): *"exchange timestamp to on-screen paint is measured per stage (ingest, internal fan-out, client render) and reported as percentiles"*, *"Given p95 exceeds 250 ms for 60 seconds, then an alert fires naming the stage that consumed the budget"*, and a compact latency indicator available in the UI. ADR-0014 §2 adds the frontend telemetry push: *"Field performance regressions in the chart engine are otherwise invisible until a user complains."* The stage allocation is fixed in `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §5.1 (parse ≤3 ms, … fan-out ≤7 ms summing to the ≤20 ms backend-internal envelope; total tick → pixel ≤250 ms).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Stage timestamping: an exchange event carries `t_exchange` (Bybit's own ts), `t_received`, `t_parsed`, `t_derived`, `t_emitted` through the internal bus, so each stage's cost is a subtraction rather than a guess. Exposed as `ingest_stage_seconds{stage}` and `ws_fanout_latency_seconds` histograms with buckets straddling the §5.1 allocations.
- Clock-offset correction: `t_exchange` is on the exchange's clock, so raw subtraction measures clock skew, not latency. Correct using the offset from `bybit_clock_drift_ms` (E08/US-MKT-009) and, until that exists, report the exchange-origin stage as `unavailable` rather than as a plausible-looking wrong number.
- `POST /api/v1/telemetry/frontend` — authenticated, strict-schema, low-rate (one aggregated payload per 10 s per session) accepting `fe_frame_time_ms` (histogram buckets, not raw samples), `fe_dropped_frames_total`, `fe_ws_decode_ms`, `fe_gpu_memory_mb`, plus `screen` and `engine_version`. Server-side rate limit and payload size cap; rejected payloads counted, never logged verbatim.
- Client-side aggregator in the web app that batches locally and drops silently when offline (telemetry must never retry-storm a degraded backend).
- Recording rules encoding the `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §2 budgets as SLO burn rates, so Grafana shows "is this getting worse" rather than raw numbers (ADR-0014 §8), consumed by E04-S01's dashboards and E04-T05's alerts.
- Budget-breach alert naming the offending stage: the alert annotation is computed from the per-stage histograms, so the notification says *which* stage consumed the budget, as US-OBS-002 requires.
- OpenTelemetry spans on exactly the two paths sanctioned by ADR-0014 §5: the order path (`http.request → oms.validate → oms.fanout → exchange.place_order → private_ws.fill`) and replay session start. Span scaffolding and context propagation ship here; the OMS/replay spans are attached by E29/E26 against this scaffolding.
- Data contract for the compact in-UI latency indicator (CMP-208 StatusBar's `latencyMs`, CMP-210 HealthChips) — the widget itself is E10's.

## Out of scope
- The StatusBar/HealthChips UI implementation (E10 App shell) — contract and design spec only here.
- Engine FPS benchmarking harness in CI — E06 Chart-engine spike owns the benchmark; this ticket receives its field telemetry.
- Tracing market-data hot loops — explicitly rejected by ADR-0014 §5 and confirmed by E04-K01.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Per-stage percentiles are reported
  Given market data is flowing for three symbols
  When the latency dashboards are queried
  Then p50/p95/p99 are available per stage (ingest parse, derive, fan-out, client decode, client paint) and the stages sum to the end-to-end figure within measurement tolerance

Scenario: Budget breach names the stage
  Given end-to-end p95 exceeds 250 ms for 60 s because fan-out is slow
  Then a Ticket-severity alert fires whose annotation names fan-out as the consuming stage, not merely "latency high"

Scenario: Clock skew is not mistaken for latency
  Given the exchange clock is 800 ms ahead of local time
  When the exchange-origin stage is computed
  Then the reported latency is offset-corrected, and if no offset measurement is available the stage reports unavailable rather than a negative or inflated value

Scenario: Frontend telemetry is bounded and safe
  Given a client posts a 5 MB payload, or posts 100 times per second, or posts an unknown field
  Then the request is rejected with 400 or 429, the rejection is counted, the payload is not logged verbatim, and no unbounded series is created in Prometheus

Scenario: Telemetry never harms the app
  Given the backend is unreachable
  When the client aggregator tries to push
  Then it drops the batch after one attempt, does not queue unboundedly, and no user-visible error appears
```

## Technical notes / design
Histogram-of-histograms is the correct shape for frontend data: clients send pre-bucketed counts, the server adds them into a server-side histogram. Sending raw frame samples would be both a cardinality disaster and a privacy smell. Label `screen` from a **closed enum** of route ids — never a free-form path, or one dynamic route id blows up cardinality.

Percentile arithmetic warning to reviewers: **percentiles do not sum**. The "stages sum to end-to-end" check is valid for p50-ish central tendency and for the *budget allocation* narrative, but the end-to-end p95 must be measured directly with a single correlated timestamp pair, not assembled from per-stage p95s. Implement the end-to-end measurement as a genuine paired measurement (a sampled 1-in-N event carrying its origin timestamp all the way to paint) and use the per-stage histograms for attribution only.

Measurement overhead ≤1% CPU (US-OBS-002 NFR) — the 1-in-N sampling for end-to-end pairing exists precisely to stay inside that.

Config keys: `CV_TELEMETRY_ENABLED`, `CV_TELEMETRY_SAMPLE_N` (default 100), `CV_OTEL_ENABLED`, `CV_OTEL_ENDPOINT`.

## Test plan
- Unit: stage-subtraction arithmetic incl. clock-offset correction and the unavailable path; negative-duration guard; payload schema validation (unknown field, oversize, wrong types, hostile `screen` value); client aggregator batching, drop-on-offline, no unbounded queue.
- Contract: `POST /telemetry/frontend` added to `22-api-openapi.yaml` and diff-checked; recording-rule output names asserted stable (dashboards depend on them).

title: Provision six Grafana dashboards as reviewed JSON in the repository
body:
## Context
As the **owner**, I want dashboards that answer "is the system healthy and is it getting worse" at a glance, so that problems are measurable rather than anecdotal (**US-OBS-001**, `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §28). ADR-0014 §3 fixes both the set and the discipline: six provisioned dashboards stored as JSON in `infra/grafana`, code-reviewed like any other artefact — *"No click-ops dashboards: if it is not in the repository, it does not exist."* This is half of R0 exit criterion 10 (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §4.3): *"Grafana shows ingestion rate, WS state, queue depth and API latency."*

## Scope / Deliverables
- `infra/grafana/provisioning/` — datasource and dashboard providers (file-based provisioning, dashboards read-only in the UI so an accidental in-browser edit cannot silently become the source of truth).
- Six dashboards per `20-architecture.md` §12.4, each as reviewed JSON:
  1. **System health** — `event_loop_lag_seconds`, CPU/RAM, `ws_connection_state`, `topic_staleness_seconds`, `ingest_queue_depth`, `health_component_state{component}`, `build_info` deploy annotations.
  2. **Market data** — messages/s per topic, `ws_message_bytes_total`, `book_resync_total{symbol,reason}`, `engine_process_seconds{engine}`, `ws_fanout_latency_seconds`.
  3. **Trading** — `order_submit_seconds`, `orders_total{state,env}`, reject reasons, `bybit_rate_remaining{endpoint_group}`, `oms_unknown_orders`, `naked_position_alerts_total` (panels authored now against declared names; populate when E29 lands).
  4. **Rules** — `rule_evaluations_total`, `rule_fires_total{rule_id}`, `rule_autodisarm_total`.
  5. **Storage** — `recorder_rows_total{stream}`, `recorder_spill_bytes`, `disk_used_ratio`, `questdb_write_seconds`, `pg_pool_in_use`, `pg_query_seconds`, retention/roll-off runs.
  6. **Frontend** — `fe_frame_time_ms`, `fe_dropped_frames_total`, `fe_ws_decode_ms`, `fe_gpu_memory_mb`, per-screen p95.
- SLO burn-rate rows on the system-health and frontend dashboards using the recording rules from E04-T06, so the top of each dashboard answers "getting worse?" before any raw gauge is read.
- `env` template variable on every dashboard, defaulting to the current environment — demo and live must never be read on the same panel by accident.
- A nightly Grafana snapshot export job (ADR-0014 mitigation for Prometheus's 15-day retention) writing to the local artefact directory for load-test and release comparisons.
- CI check: every dashboard JSON lints, references only declared datasource uids, and every panel query references a metric present in the E04-T03 catalogue (a panel querying a typo'd metric renders an empty graph that reads as "healthy" — the most dangerous possible dashboard defect).

## Out of scope
- Grafana authentication/SSO beyond the private-bind default (infra/E03 scope).
- In-app health UI (SCR-143) — E42, designed in E04-D01.
- Alert rules — E04-T05 (Grafana alerting is not used; Prometheus + Alertmanager is the decided path).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given a clean docker compose stack is brought up
When Grafana starts
Then all six dashboards are present without any manual import step, each bound to the provisioned Prometheus datasource

Given the system is running with three symbols ingesting
When the System health and Market data dashboards are opened
Then ingestion rate, WS connection state, queue depth and API latency all display live data with units and thresholds, satisfying R0 exit criterion 10

Given a panel references a metric name that does not exist in the catalogue
When CI runs the dashboard lint check
Then the build fails naming the panel and the metric, rather than shipping a permanently empty graph

Given a dashboard is edited in the Grafana UI
When the container restarts
Then the repository version is restored, and the UI shows the dashboard as provisioned/read-only so the edit could not have been mistaken for persistent

Given the env template variable is set to demo
When any panel is read
Then only demo-labelled series are shown and the dashboard title bar states the environment
```

## Technical notes / design
Write dashboard JSON by hand or generate it with grafanalib and commit the output — either way the committed JSON is the reviewed artefact. Pin `schemaVersion` and strip volatile fields (`id`, `version`, `iteration`) in a pre-commit hook, otherwise every export produces a meaningless diff and reviewers stop reading them, which defeats the entire "reviewed like code" premise.

Panel thresholds must be sourced from `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §2 rather than eyeballed, so a green panel means "inside budget" and not "looks fine". Use `$__rate_interval` for counter rates (a fixed `[1m]` breaks silently when the scrape interval changes).

Deploy annotations come from `build_info` changes (E04-T04) — correlating a regression with a deploy is the most common real-world dashboard question.

## Test plan
- CI lint: JSON schema validity, datasource uid resolution, metric-existence check against the catalogue, `$__rate_interval` usage, threshold presence on budget-bearing panels.
- Integration: compose stack, headless check that each dashboard renders with ≥1 non-empty panel under a synthetic load.
- Manual: reviewer walks each dashboard against `20-architecture.md` §12.4's stated purpose.
- Regression: snapshot-diff test on the committed JSON to catch accidental UI-export churn.

## Security notes
Grafana binds privately only (`20-architecture.md` §13.1 — loopback/WSL-internal, no public ingress); default admin credentials must be replaced at provisioning time and the credential injected from the environment, never committed (gitleaks-covered). Dashboards must not render label values that constitute disclosure (no account ids beyond an opaque short id, no order ids). Anonymous access disabled. Snapshot exports stay on the local machine and are excluded from CI artefact upload (SR-124 spirit).

## Accessibility notes
Dashboards are an operator surface and still fall under `05-accessibility-standard.md`: every panel carries a text title and unit; panels conveying state use a threshold **plus** a stat value, never colour alone; avoid red/green-only encodings on the system-health row (use shape/label or an explicit state word). Colour-blind-safe palette selected at the dashboard level.

## Performance notes
Dashboard queries must not overload a degraded Prometheus: default time range 1 h, `max_data_points` capped, no unbounded `topk` over high-cardinality labels. The System-health dashboard must render in < 3 s against 15 days of data.

## Observability
Self-referential: the System-health dashboard includes `prometheus_rule_group_last_duration_seconds`, `alertmanager_notifications_failed_total` and the watchdog alert state, so the observability stack's own health is visible on the first dashboard an operator opens.
