title: Generate a secret-scanned, size-capped diagnostic support bundle
body:
## Context
As the **owner**, I want to generate a diagnostic bundle, so that I can debug an incident after the fact (**US-OBS-007**, Should, `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §28). This matters more here than in most systems because ADR-0014 deliberately defers Loki: with no centralised log search, post-incident analysis means collecting the right files for a window, and doing that by hand under pressure is how secrets end up in a zip. The story's own acceptance criteria make the safety property explicit: *"the bundle is scanned for secret patterns before being written, and generation fails loudly if any are found"*.

SCR-143 exposes the entry point as `[ export diagnostics ]` and SCR-119 (Help & about) and SCR-156 (application error boundary) also reference bundle generation (`docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md`).

## Scope / Deliverables
- `POST /api/v1/admin/support-bundle` with `{from, to}` (max window 24 h), `x-rbac: {permissions: [admin:read]}`, returning a job id; `GET /api/v1/admin/support-bundle/{id}` for status and a local download path. Endpoint added to `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` before implementation (interface-first rule).
- Bundle contents: structured logs for the window, a Prometheus snapshot of the key series, the health report (`GET /admin/health`), recent `system_events` rows, active alerts, build-info, and configuration **with secrets removed** (allow-list of config keys, not a deny-list — a deny-list silently ships every newly added secret key).
- **Pre-write secret scan**: the assembled bundle is scanned in a temporary location with the gitleaks rule set plus the E04-T01 redaction patterns; on any hit the bundle is destroyed, generation fails with error code `BUNDLE_SECRET_DETECTED`, and the finding is logged with the file and rule name but **not** the matched value.
- Size cap (default 200 MB) with newest-first truncation; the manifest states explicitly what was truncated and over what window, per the story's third scenario.
- Bundle written **only to the local machine**, never uploaded; audited as a `health.diagnostics_exported` event (SCR-143's stated audit action) with actor, window and resulting size.
- Manifest file listing every included artefact with a sha256, so a bundle shared later can be shown to be unmodified.

## Out of scope
- Any automatic upload, cloud storage or third-party transmission — prohibited by the story NFR.
- The SCR-119 / SCR-143 / SCR-156 UI affordances — E42/E10; this story delivers the API and the audit event.
- Bundling QuestDB or Parquet market data (size-prohibitive and not diagnostic); only metrics snapshots and logs.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given the owner requests a bundle for a 2-hour window
When generation completes
Then the archive contains logs, a metrics snapshot, config with secrets removed, the health report, recent system_events and active alerts, plus a manifest with a sha256 per artefact, and an audit row health.diagnostics_exported is written

Given a log line in the window somehow contains an unredacted API secret
When the pre-write scan runs
Then generation fails with BUNDLE_SECRET_DETECTED, no archive is left on disk, the failure names the offending file and rule, and the matched secret value is not written to the log or the error response

Given the requested window would produce 4 GB
When generation runs
Then the bundle is capped at the configured limit, the most recent data is preserved, and the manifest states which artefacts were truncated and from what point

Given a Manager (not Owner) requests a bundle
Then the response is 403, no bundle is generated, and the denied attempt is audited

Given bundle generation is already running
When a second request arrives
Then it is rejected with 409 rather than running concurrently and doubling disk and CPU pressure on a system that is by hypothesis already unwell
```

## Technical notes / design
Generate into a `0700` temporary directory on the same filesystem, scan, then atomically move into place — never assemble in the final location, or a failed scan leaves a secret-bearing archive behind for the window between write and delete. Stream into the archive rather than materialising the whole bundle in memory (a 200 MB cap must not mean a 200 MB RSS spike on a degraded box).

Config allow-list: enumerate the safe keys explicitly (`CV_ENV`, `CV_LOG_LEVEL`, bind addresses, feature-flag states, retention settings, version pins). Anything not on the list is emitted as `<omitted>` with its key name retained — the *shape* of the config is diagnostic even when the value must not appear.

Run generation as a background job with a bounded worker (concurrency 1, hence the 409) and a hard timeout; a support bundle that pins a CPU during an incident is a self-inflicted second incident.

Error codes: `BUNDLE_SECRET_DETECTED`, `BUNDLE_WINDOW_TOO_LARGE`, `BUNDLE_ALREADY_RUNNING`, `BUNDLE_DISK_INSUFFICIENT` (refuse if free space < 2× the cap).

## Test plan
- Unit: config allow-list filtering (incl. a newly added unknown secret key being omitted by default); truncation preserving newest data; manifest sha256 correctness; window validation; concurrency guard.
- Unit (security-critical): planted-canary test — a secret is deliberately injected into a source log and the scan must fail generation and leave no artefact on disk. This test is a required CI check.
- Contract: new endpoints validated against `22-api-openapi.yaml`.
- Integration: full bundle generated in the compose stack, extracted, contents asserted, audit row asserted.
- Chaos: disk full mid-generation → clean failure with `BUNDLE_DISK_INSUFFICIENT`, temp directory cleaned up, no partial archive.
- Coverage ≥85%.

## Security notes
This is the epic's highest-risk surface: it deliberately aggregates operational data into one portable file. Controls: RBAC `admin:read` (Owner-scoped), allow-listed config, mandatory pre-write secret scan with fail-closed behaviour, no automatic upload (story NFR), audited generation (`health.diagnostics_exported`), restrictive file permissions (`0600`), and exclusion from any CI artefact upload (SR-124). Threats: K1 (key material in logs propagating into a bundle), D3 (operational-detail disclosure), plus the abuse case "a Manager exfiltrates operational state" — covered in E04-X02. Data classification: Confidential.

## Accessibility notes
N/A for this API-only story. The consuming UI affordance (SCR-143 `[ export diagnostics ]`, SCR-119) must announce completion and failure via a live region and expose the failure reason as text — specified in E04-D01 and implemented in E42.

## Performance notes
Generation must not breach the frame/latency budgets of a running system: bounded concurrency 1, streamed I/O, nice'd background execution, hard timeout 120 s, refuse when free disk < 2× cap. Target: a 2 h window bundle completes in < 30 s.

## Observability
`support_bundle_generations_total{result}`, `support_bundle_duration_seconds`, `support_bundle_bytes`, plus a `system_events` row per generation and a Ticket-severity alert on `result="secret_detected"` — a scan hit means the redaction filter failed somewhere and must be investigated, not merely retried.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin criteria automated, including the planted-canary test as a required check.
- [ ] `22-api-openapi.yaml` updated and contract test green.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85%.
- [ ] Security engineer review + manual abuse-case check (attempt generation as Manager; attempt to smuggle a secret through config).
- [ ] Audit event verified present in `audit_log`.
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded.
- [ ] Demo: bundle generated and opened at Sprint Review with the secret-scan failure path shown.
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded (`CV_SUPPORT_BUNDLE_ENABLED`, default on in all environments).
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue.

`E04-T02` (correlation ids make the collected logs worth collecting), `E04-T04` (health report and `system_events` are bundle contents). Reuses the E04-T01 redaction patterns for the scan.

title: Write alert runbooks and reconcile ADR-0014 with the shipped observability stack
body:
## Context
ADR-0014 §6 states the rule without qualification: *"Every alert links to a runbook section in `07-release-and-prr.md`. An alert without a runbook is not allowed to be created."* E04-T05 enforces the link mechanically in CI; this ticket writes the destinations and closes the epic's documentation obligations, including the R0 PRR-lite requirement for a "dev environment rebuild" runbook (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §4.4).

## Scope / Deliverables
- A runbook section in `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md` for **every** alert rule shipped in E04-T05, each with a fixed structure: what fired, what the user impact is, what is still safe (SCR-143's outage state says "Native stops on the exchange are unaffected" — runbooks must say the equivalent), first three diagnostic commands, remediation, escalation, and how to verify recovery.
- Runbook for **dev environment rebuild** (PRR-lite gate item).
- Runbook for "observability stack itself is down" — what to trust when Prometheus, Grafana or Alertmanager is the thing that failed, including the watchdog's meaning (no watchdog notification = pipeline dead, not = all well).
- ADR-0014 reconciliation: an addendum recording what actually shipped versus what was decided, including the E04-K01 overhead numbers and any catalogue/label deviations.
- `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §12 updated to match the shipped metric catalogue, log field set, dashboards and alert policy.
- `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` updated for R11 (alert reliability) with the residual risk after this epic.
- A one-page "observability contract for module authors" in the repo docs: how to register a metric, which labels are permitted, how to add a probe, how to get an alert approved — so E08/E09/E16/E29/E35 comply by default instead of by review.

## Out of scope

title: Design the system-health, incident-log and degraded-state surfaces (SCR-143, SCR-144, SCR-152, SCR-156)
body:
## Context
E04 defines the data contracts that four user-facing surfaces consume, and under the design-ahead rule (`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` — design runs ≥2 sprints ahead; no frontend screen work starts until its design is signed off) those surfaces must be designed now, in R0, even though they are built later in E42/E10. Designing them alongside the API is also the only way to catch contract gaps early: SCR-143's requirement that *"the page works when the backend is partially down"* is a design constraint that shapes E04-T04's per-component `last_good_at` and independent-probe-timeout behaviour.

Surfaces in scope (`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`, `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md`):
- **SCR-143** Admin: system health (US-ADMIN-011, US-OBS-001, US-OBS-002)
- **SCR-144** Admin: incident / connectivity log (US-OBS-003, US-OBS-006)
- **SCR-152** Disconnected / reconnecting state (US-OBS-004, US-POS-008, US-MKT-007)
- **SCR-156** Application error boundary (US-OBS-003, US-OBS-007)

## Scope / Deliverables
- **UX research (light, 1 session)**: interview the owner on incident triage — what is the first question asked when something feels wrong, and what "still safe" means to them while degraded. This directly determines tile ordering on SCR-143 and the wording of the outage state.
- **Wireframes → hi-fi in Figma** for all four screens, covering every state named in the catalogue:
  - SCR-143: all-green · degraded (per-subsystem amber with reason + last-good timestamp) · outage (red, ongoing incident, what is still safe — e.g. "Native stops on the exchange are unaffected") · maintenance window.
  - SCR-144: open vs resolved · filters by subsystem/severity/date · expandable detail rows · acknowledge action · export · empty state · trading-impact correlation ("12 orders rejected during this window") where derivable.
  - SCR-152: reconnect overlay states incl. retry-exhausted.
  - SCR-156: crash boundary with correlation id and a route to support-bundle generation (US-OBS-007).
- **Design-system contributions** to E05: **CMP-178** SystemHealthTile (Ok/Warning/Danger + sparkline), **CMP-210** HealthChips, **CMP-092** DegradedModeBanner, **CMP-076** ConnectionStatus, **CMP-077** ReconnectOverlay, **CMP-207** BuildFooter — specs, tokens, states and Storybook story lists, filed as design-system entries rather than one-off screens (DoR §3.1).
- **Motion spec**: state transitions between healthy/degraded/down must be legible but never attention-grabbing enough to be muted by the operator; define reduced-motion equivalents.
- **Content design**: the state vocabulary (`ok`/`warning`/`degraded`/`down`/`not deployed`) used identically in the API (E04-T04), the chips, the tiles and the alert notifications (E04-T05) — one vocabulary, defined once.
- **Handoff pack**: redlines, token references, the component-to-API field mapping (each tile → `HealthReport.components[].{state,latency_ms,detail,last_good_at}`), and the empty/loading/error matrix.

## Out of scope
- Building the screens (E42 Admin, E10 App shell).
- Grafana dashboard visual design — a third-party surface, configured not designed (E04-S01).
- Any Android/mobile layout (out of scope per owner decision 2026-09-14).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given the SCR-143 design is presented for sign-off
When it is checked against the screen's design sign-off acceptance checklist in 14-screens-catalogue.md
Then every listed item is satisfied: tiles for ingestion lag, public WS, private WS per account, REST latency, recorder, DB tiers, rule engine, algo engine and chart-engine FPS; each tile showing a number with units plus a state word; degraded and down states drawn per tile with what the user should expect to stop working; a historical sparkline per tile with a table alternative; a link to the incident log; and a layout that works when the backend is partially down

Given any health state is rendered
When a colour-blind simulation and a greyscale render are applied
Then the state remains unambiguous, because state is always a word and a value, never a dot colour alone

Given the SCR-144 design is reviewed
Then columns include time, subsystem, severity (as text), message, duration and resolution; long messages expand into a detail row rather than truncating silently; and open/resolved, filter, acknowledge, export and empty states are all drawn

Given a designer hands off to engineering
Then every visual element maps to a named field of the HealthReport or Incident schema in 22-api-openapi.yaml, and any field the design needs that does not yet exist is filed as a comment on E04-T04 before sign-off

Given the design is signed off
Then sign-off is recorded by the CDO or delegate with the date, and the ticket Status is Done at least 2 sprints before the consuming frontend story starts
```

## Technical notes / design
The defining constraint is that this screen is read when the system is unwell: every tile must resolve independently (no shared loading gate), and the page must degrade to "I could not reach the backend, here is the last thing I knew and when" rather than to a spinner. Design the *unreachable-backend* variant first and the all-green variant last — the reverse order produces a beautiful dashboard that is blank exactly when it is needed.

Density follows the design-system density tokens (`docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`); this is an information-dense operator screen, so use the compact density variant but verify touch/click target minimums still meet WCAG 2.2 AA target-size guidance.

## Test plan
- Design QA is a separate ticket (E04-D02); this ticket's verification is the per-screen sign-off checklist in `14-screens-catalogue.md` plus a contrast/colour-blind pass on every state.
- Prototype test: one moderated walkthrough with the owner using a clickable prototype of the degraded and outage states, confirming they can answer "what is broken, what is still safe, what do I do" in under 30 s.

## Security notes
The designs must not surface secret material or full account identifiers: account references on SCR-143/SCR-147-adjacent tiles use a truncated opaque id (per SR-005, no more than the first 4 characters of a key id may ever be shown). The incident log's detail rows must be designed assuming the underlying `system_events.details` is operator-visible but must never be designed to show raw exchange payloads verbatim. Support-bundle generation from SCR-156 must be designed as an explicit, confirmed, audited action — not a one-click background side effect.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`). Specific commitments: each subsystem is a labelled row/tile with a text status (SCR-143 a11y note — "no reliance on dot colour"); every sparkline has a table alternative; severity in SCR-144 is text; the reconnect overlay (CMP-077) is `role="alertdialog"`, non-dismissible with a keyboard-operable retry and no false "OK" affordance; status regions announce at most once per state change, not per heartbeat (CMP-076 announcement-throttling contract); focus order and visible focus states specified; contrast ≥4.5:1 for text and ≥3:1 for state indicators in all three themes (dark, light, high-contrast).

## Performance notes
Design within SCR-143's budget: tiles subscribe to the WS `system` topic at 1 Hz and the page must stay under 2 ms scripting per frame; SCR-144 must scroll 10k rows without exceeding 8 ms scripting per frame, so the design must assume row virtualisation and avoid per-row animation or shadow effects that defeat it.

## Observability
Specify the analytics/audit events the screens emit, matching the catalogue: `health.diagnostics_exported` (audited), `incident.log_viewed`, `incident.exported`, `incident.acknowledged` (audited).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Hi-fi Figma frames for all four screens, all states, all three themes.
- [ ] Per-screen sign-off checklists in `14-screens-catalogue.md` fully satisfied.
- [ ] Design-system entries for CMP-076, CMP-077, CMP-092, CMP-178, CMP-207, CMP-210 accepted by the design-system team into E05's backlog.
- [ ] Motion + reduced-motion specs included.
- [ ] Content/state vocabulary agreed with backend (E04-T04) and alerting (E04-T05).
- [ ] Handoff pack published with component↔API field mapping; engineering walkthrough held.
- [ ] a11y pre-review passed with the accessibility specialist (contrast, non-colour-redundancy, focus, announcements).
- [ ] CDO (or delegate) sign-off recorded with date; Status Done ≥2 sprints before the consuming E42/E10 story starts.
- [ ] `14-screens-catalogue.md` / `15-component-catalogue.md` updated if the design diverged from the written spec.

## Dependencies
`E05-D01` (Build Figma Foundations file: token variables for the three themes) — the token variables must exist to design these frames against. The dependency is pinned to that specific ticket rather than the whole `E05` epic, because only the Foundations file is actually required.

**Why Sprint 01, outside E04's S02–S03 roadmap window.** `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` requires a design ticket to land **two sprints before the consuming FE story**. The consumers here are `E04-T04` (health / readiness contract) and `E04-S01` (Grafana + system-health surfaces) in Sprint 03, plus the shared degraded-state surfaces reused by E42 and E10. Sprint 01 is therefore the scheduled-correct slot: it sits immediately *preceding* E04's declared train window rather than inside it, which is intentional and is recorded in the sprint-window reconciliation table on the `E04` epic ticket.

**Same-sprint dependency risk and its mitigation.** `E05-D01` is also Sprint 01, so this is a same-sprint dependency. It is accepted with these controls: (a) this ticket only needs the colour / spacing / type primitives, which `E05-D01` publishes as draft variables in the first half of the sprint, so the two run staggered inside one sprint rather than in parallel from day one; (b) no code depends on this ticket until Sprint 03, so a one-sprint slip of `E05-D01` pushes this ticket to Sprint 02 and still clears `E04-T04` without moving the train; (c) any token added or renamed later by `E05-D02` (Sprint 02) is re-applied to these frames during `E04-D02` design QA in Sprint 03, which is the formal sign-off gate. Escalation: if `E05-D01` has not published draft variables by the Sprint-01 midpoint, the epic owner re-plans this ticket into Sprint 02.

Informs and is informed by `E04-T04` (health contract); any field missing from the health payload is raised on that ticket before sign-off.

## Context
DoD §3.2 makes design QA default-on for net-new UI and mandates an a11y pass (axe-core CI green plus a manual screen-reader spot-check). E04's own UI surface in R0 is limited — the health chrome components and the Grafana operator surface — but the design specs from E04-D01 and the API-level state vocabulary must be verified *now*, while the contracts are still cheap to change, rather than at E42 when the screens are built and the vocabulary is embedded in three places.

## Scope / Deliverables

- Accessibility review of the same components: axe-core zero violations in Storybook; manual screen-reader pass (NVDA on Windows as primary, VoiceOver spot-check); keyboard-only operation; focus order and visible focus; announcement throttling verified (CMP-076's contract: `degraded`/`offline` announce once via `role="alert"`, **not** on every heartbeat — verify by driving 60 heartbeats and counting announcements).
- Contrast verification across dark, light and high-contrast themes for every state token used by health surfaces.
- Colour-blind and greyscale verification that no state is distinguishable by colour alone.
- Review of the alert notification text from E04-T05 as a content surface: severity is a word, no colour/emoji-only meaning.
- Grafana dashboard a11y spot-check (E04-S01): panel titles, units, non-colour-alone thresholds, colour-blind-safe palette.
- Findings either fixed in-sprint or filed as Bugs with `priority/*` set, per DoD §3.2.

## Out of scope

- Re-designing anything (findings are filed, not redesigned here).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given each of the six components is rendered in Storybook in every declared state and theme
When axe-core runs
Then zero violations are reported, and the run link is attached to the ticket per the a11y run-link guard

Given the ConnectionStatus component receives 60 heartbeat updates while in the degraded state
When screen-reader output is captured
Then exactly one announcement is made for the state change, not sixty

Given every health state token is rendered in dark, light and high-contrast themes
When contrast is measured
Then text meets ≥4.5:1 and non-text state indicators meet ≥3:1 in all three themes, with any failure filed as a Bug

Given a greyscale render of every state
When a reviewer who has not seen the colour version reads it
Then they can correctly name each state, because state is always a word plus a value

Given a keyboard-only user encounters the ReconnectOverlay

```

## Technical notes / design
The announcement-throttling check is the one most likely to be skipped and the one most likely to be broken: a `role="alert"` region bound to a value that updates at 1 Hz turns a screen reader into an unusable metronome, and it passes axe-core cleanly. Test it behaviourally, not statically.

Use the design-system's visual-regression baseline (E05) so token drift is caught by diff rather than by eye.

- Automated: axe-core across all Storybook stories in CI; visual-regression snapshots per state and theme; a unit test asserting announcement count under repeated updates.
- Manual: NVDA pass over each component; keyboard-only traversal; greyscale and colour-blind simulation review; contrast measurement with a tool, recorded per token pair.
- Evidence: run links and screenshots attached to the ticket.

Verify no component renders more than the first 4 characters of any key id and that no `detail` string is rendered as HTML (CMP components must not use `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` — SR-127). Confirm the BuildFooter exposes version/commit but no internal hostnames or paths.

The entire ticket is the a11y pass: WCAG 2.2 AA per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`, covering perceivable (contrast, non-colour-redundancy), operable (keyboard, focus, target size), understandable (state vocabulary consistent across chips, tiles, banners and alerts) and robust (roles, names, live-region politeness levels).

title: Write and execute the black-box test plan and alert drill for the observability baseline
body:
## Context
R0 exit criterion 10 (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §4.3) requires that *"Grafana shows ingestion rate, WS state, queue depth and API latency; a synthetic alert fires and is received"* — an assertion that must be executed and recorded by QA, not asserted by the implementer. `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` requires a black-box test plan per feature, and DoD §8 forbids silently skipping QA sign-off.

The specific quality risk this ticket exists to address: observability defects are *invisible by construction*. A dashboard panel querying a typo'd metric renders an empty graph that looks like calm; an alert rule with a label matcher that matches nothing never fires and reads as "no problems". Black-box testing here must therefore be adversarial — prove each signal fires, not merely that the system looks healthy.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A written black-box test plan covering US-OBS-001, US-OBS-002, US-OBS-003, US-OBS-004, US-OBS-005, US-OBS-007, mapped scenario-by-scenario to the Gherkin in `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §28 and to the epic's children.
- **Alert drill matrix**: every Page and Ticket rule from E04-T05 is *deliberately fired at least once* in staging and its runbook walked — ADR-0014's Validation section makes this a PRR item; this ticket executes the R0 subset and hands the remainder to E45/R4.
- **Negative drills**: for each rule, a near-miss series that must *not* fire (threshold minus epsilon, duration minus epsilon), proving the rule discriminates rather than merely triggering.
- Dashboard verification: each of the six dashboards opened under synthetic load; each panel confirmed to show data or be explicitly annotated "awaits module X"; no silently-empty panel accepted.
- Health-endpoint matrix: each dependency stopped in turn, asserting `/health/live`, `/health/ready` and `/admin/health` behave per E04-T04's criteria, including the slow-probe isolation case.
- Logging verification: canary secrets pushed through every logging path (app, stdlib, third-party, traceback) and confirmed absent from output; correlation id followed end to end through a request; runtime log-level override raised, scoped and confirmed self-reverting.
- Support-bundle verification: happy path, secret-detection failure path, truncation path, RBAC denial, concurrent-request rejection.
- E2E suite additions (Playwright where UI exists; API-level otherwise) for the health endpoints and the telemetry endpoint's rejection behaviours, added to the CI regression pack.
- k6 script exercising `/metrics` scrape latency at full cardinality and the frontend-telemetry endpoint at expected session load.
- QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per scenario.

## Out of scope
- Full chaos/failure drills as a release gate (US-OBS-006) — E45.
- Exploratory testing — E04-Q02.
- White-box unit/contract testing — owned by the implementing tickets.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given the black-box test plan is written
When it is reviewed against 11-user-stories.md §28
Then every Gherkin scenario of US-OBS-001..005 and US-OBS-007 maps to at least one numbered test case, and every case states its expected observable result in advance

Given every alert rule shipped in E04-T05
When the drill matrix is executed in staging
Then each rule has fired at least once, the notification was received, its runbook was walked and found executable, and the result is recorded per rule

Given a near-miss series just below each rule's threshold and duration
When it is injected
Then the rule does not fire, proving it discriminates; any rule that fires on the near-miss is filed as a Bug

Given each of the six dashboards under synthetic load
When every panel is inspected
Then no panel is silently empty: it either shows data or carries an explicit "awaits module X" annotation, and any unannotated empty panel is filed as a Bug

Given canary secrets are pushed through all four logging paths at DEBUG
When captured output is searched
Then zero canaries are found; a single hit is a priority/p0-critical Bug

Given Prometheus is stopped for 10 minutes
When the period is reviewed afterwards
Then fallback snapshot log entries exist for the window, so the gap is not invisible
```

## Technical notes / design
Drive alert drills by injecting synthetic series rather than by breaking real components where possible (faster, repeatable, and it isolates "the rule works" from "the failure is detectable") — but execute at least the Postgres-down and WS-down drills against genuinely stopped components, because synthetic injection cannot prove the *metric* reacts to the real failure. Both halves are needed: synthetic proves the rule, real proves the signal.

Record each drill with timestamps (condition injected → alert received) so the ≤60 s delivery expectation is evidenced rather than assumed.

## Test plan
This ticket *is* the test plan. Layers exercised: E2E (health, telemetry endpoints), integration (compose stack with dependencies stopped), load (k6 scrape and telemetry), manual/exploratory-adjacent (drill execution and runbook walking). Fixtures: synthetic Prometheus series generator; canary-secret fixture set shared with E04-T01's unit tests; a recorded 10-minute market-data fixture for the dashboard load.

## Security notes
Canary secrets used in testing must be obviously fake and distinctively prefixed so a leak of the *test* fixture is harmless and greppable. Drills that fire security alerts (failed-login spike, audit-chain failure) must be coordinated with the Security engineer so a drill is never mistaken for a real incident — and, equally, so a real incident during a drill window is not dismissed as the drill. Record drill windows in `system_events`.

## Accessibility notes
The QA pass includes verifying that alert notification text and dashboard panels convey state without relying on colour (the deeper a11y review is E04-D02); any finding is filed as a Bug with the `a11y` label.

## Performance notes
Validate `/metrics` scrape < 50 ms at full declared cardinality and alert delivery ≤ 60 s for Page severity; record both numbers against `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.

## Observability
Test artefacts (drill reports) are retained as release evidence per US-OBS-006's reporting principle, even though the full drill programme is E45's.

- [ ] Test plan written, reviewed by the QA lead and the epic owner.
- [ ] Every case executed with pass/fail recorded; failures filed as Bugs with priority.

title: Run an exploratory charter on observability blind spots and build the regression pack
body:
## Context
Scripted tests (E04-Q01) prove that the signals we thought of work. The residual risk in an observability baseline is the signal nobody thought of — the subsystem that can fail in a way no metric expresses, the state that renders as healthy because the probe measures the wrong thing. That is exploratory territory, and it is best spent *before* R1 builds twenty modules on top of this foundation.

This ticket also assembles the durable regression pack so the epic's guarantees survive later refactors, and closes the epic's QA obligations for the R0 epic-level sign-off (Epic DoD: *"an Epic-level regression/exploratory pass executed and recorded, not just child-ticket QA"*).

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Exploratory charter 1 — "Lie detector"**: *Explore the system's health reporting with the goal of making it report healthy while something is genuinely broken.* Time-boxed 4 h. Techniques: stop a component after its probe has cached a good result; saturate a queue without crossing a threshold; desync a topic while its connection stays up; fill disk to 79%; stall a writer without erroring.
- **Exploratory charter 2 — "Silence detector"**: *Explore the alerting path with the goal of producing a real failure that generates no notification.* 4 h. Techniques: break Alertmanager's outbound path; fire during a quiet-hours window; produce a condition whose metric is emitted by a module that is down (so the series goes absent rather than crossing a threshold — the classic `absent()` gap); fire two alerts whose inhibition rules suppress each other.
- **Exploratory charter 3 — "Leak hunt"**: *Explore every output surface (logs, metrics labels, health details, alert payloads, support bundle, dashboard panels) for secret or PII exposure.* 3 h, run jointly with the Security engineer feeding E04-X02.
- A **regression pack** added to CI: the canary-secret suite, the health-matrix suite, the near-miss alert suite (promtool), the dashboard metric-existence check, the cardinality-guard test and the announcement-throttling test — the set of assertions whose silent breakage would leave the system blind.
- A written blind-spot report: conditions the system genuinely cannot currently detect, each either accepted with a rationale or filed as a ticket against the owning epic (E08 ingestion, E29 OMS, E16 recorder).
- Epic-level QA sign-off for E04.

## Out of scope
- Implementing the fixes found (filed as Bugs/Tasks against the owning ticket).
- Full chaos drills (E45).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given charter 1 is executed for its full time box
When findings are reviewed
Then every technique attempted is documented with its outcome, and any case where the system reported healthy while broken is filed as a Bug at priority/p1-high or above

Given charter 2 discovers a real failure that produces no notification
Then the gap is either closed in-sprint (for example by adding an absent() guard or an inhibition-rule correction) or accepted in writing by the Owner with the residual risk recorded in 32-risk-register.md

Given charter 3 is executed across all six output surfaces
Then each surface is explicitly cleared or has a finding filed, and the results are handed to E04-X02 as input to the security review

Given the regression pack is added to CI
When any of its assertions is deliberately broken in a scratch branch
Then CI fails, proving the pack is actually wired in and not merely present

Given the epic-level pass is complete
Then a QA sign-off comment is posted on E04 listing scenarios covered, defects found, defects outstanding and residual risk
```

## Technical notes / design
Exploratory work is documented session-style (charter, duration, coverage areas, notes, bugs, obstacles, follow-ups) so it is auditable and repeatable, not anecdotal. The most productive technique in charter 1 is attacking the *caching* introduced for performance: a 2 s probe cache and a 1 Hz UI poll create a window where the displayed state is stale by design — establish that the window is bounded and that `last_good_at` makes the staleness visible rather than hiding it.

For charter 2, the highest-yield case is the absent-series gap: when a module dies, its metric stops existing, and a rule of the form `metric > threshold` can never fire. Confirm every such rule has an `absent()` companion — a systematic, checkable property rather than a one-off finding.

## Test plan
Charters as above. Regression-pack verification is itself tested by deliberate breakage in a scratch branch (the "is the smoke alarm wired in" check). Fixtures reused from E04-Q01.

## Security notes
Charter 3 is a security-adjacent exercise run with the Security engineer; findings feed E04-X02's review and, if a secret is found in any output surface, a `priority/p0-critical` Bug with the `security` label is filed immediately and the exposure window assessed (which environments, which retention, who could have read it).

## Accessibility notes
Exploratory pass includes a keyboard-only and screen-reader traversal of any observability UI available at this point (the chrome components from E04-D02); findings filed with the `a11y` label. Full audit is E47 for the app as a whole.

## Performance notes
Charters must not be run against an environment where a performance measurement is being taken for the record — schedule around E04-K01/T06 benchmark runs, or the benchmark measures the exploration.

## Observability
The blind-spot report is the deliverable that most directly improves observability: it enumerates what the system cannot currently see.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All three charters executed within their time boxes and documented session-style.
- [ ] Findings triaged: fixed, filed with priority, or accepted in writing with a risk-register entry.
- [ ] Regression pack merged into CI and verified by deliberate breakage.
- [ ] Blind-spot report published and follow-ups filed against owning epics.
- [ ] Epic-level QA sign-off posted on E04.
- [ ] `32-risk-register.md` updated for R11 residual risk.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue.

**Sprint-window justification (Sprint 04 vs E04's declared window S02–S03).** `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` line 104/187 allocates E04 the window **S02–S03**, which prices and schedules the *engineering build*. This ticket runs an exploratory charter and builds a regression pack **over shipped observability code**, all of which only exists once `E04-T05`, `E04-S01` and `E04-Q01` complete at the end of Sprint 03. Scheduling it inside S02–S03 would force exploration against half-provisioned dashboards and an unrouted Alertmanager, so every finding would be an artefact of incompleteness rather than a real blind spot; the epic QA sign-off required by `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 is by definition a post-build gate. title: STRIDE threat model for the observability baseline
body:
## Context
The planning brief makes a STRIDE model mandatory per epic, and `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §13.1 requires the artefact to live beside the epic in the backlog. Observability is an unusual security surface: it exists to *collect and expose* information about a system that handles API keys and order flow, so its failure modes are largely information-disclosure failures. `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5 already rates "key secret written to application logs, exception traces, HTTP debug dumps" (K1) as **High**, and lists telemetry as asset **A-17** ("Secrets leaking through logs; order intent disclosure").

This ticket runs first in the epic, before E04-T01 freezes the redaction rule set, so the model shapes the implementation instead of grading it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A STRIDE model over the E04 trust boundaries: application process → stdout/log files; application → Prometheus (`/metrics`); Prometheus → Grafana; Alertmanager → the owner's out-of-band channel (**data leaving the box** — the only egress in the epic); operator → `/admin/health`, `/admin/incidents`, support bundle; browser → `/telemetry/frontend` (inbound, untrusted).
- Per-category analysis with at least the following seeded threats, each rated (likelihood × impact) with controls and residual risk, in the table format of `04-security-program.md` §5:
  - **S**poofing: forged inbound `X-Correlation-Id` poisoning log attribution; an unauthenticated scraper reaching `/metrics`; a spoofed alert notification.
  - **T**ampering: an attacker editing a Grafana dashboard so a panel never shows the breach; silencing an Alertmanager rule; deleting log files; modifying alert rules without review.
  - **R**epudiation: operator actions (log-level override, support-bundle export, incident acknowledgement) not audited.
  - **I**nformation disclosure: secrets in logs (K1), secrets in a support bundle, order-intent inference from metric labels, component `detail` strings leaking connection strings, alert payloads carrying account/order identifiers off-box, an exposed Grafana or `/metrics` port.
  - **D**enial of service: log-volume flood from a DEBUG override; cardinality explosion from an unbounded label; telemetry-endpoint flood; support-bundle generation exhausting disk/CPU during an incident.
  - **E**levation of privilege: a Viewer reaching `/admin/health` detail or the log-level override; the telemetry endpoint accepting data that influences server behaviour.
- Mapping of each threat to the existing security requirements (SR-006, SR-007, SR-120…SR-126, SR-002, SR-005, SR-124) and identification of any gap requiring a **new** SR — proposed as a diff to `04-security-program.md`.
- Explicit abuse-case list handed to E04-X02 for verification.
- Data-classification table for every artefact the epic produces: logs, metrics, traces, dashboards, alert payloads, support bundles, `system_events` rows.

## Out of scope
- Threat models for auth/RBAC (E09), the exchange boundary (E08) or supply chain (E03) — separately required by `30-release-roadmap.md` §4.4.
- Penetration testing (R4 / E43).

## Acceptance criteria
- A STRIDE table exists covering all six categories across every listed trust boundary, with likelihood, impact, controls and residual risk per threat, in the house format.
- Every High or Critical residual risk has either a control landing inside E04 (linked to the specific child ticket) or a written, Owner-signed accepted-risk entry with a date.
- Every threat maps to an existing SR, or a new SR is proposed with a verification method; the proposed diff to `04-security-program.md` is reviewed.
- The abuse-case list is handed to E04-X02 and to E04-Q02's charter 3.
- The model is reviewed and signed off by the Security engineer and the Architect.
- `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` updated if a new risk is surfaced.

## Technical notes / design
Two threats deserve disproportionate attention because they are easy to under-rate:
1. **Alert egress.** Alertmanager is the only component in this epic that sends data off the box, to a third-party channel, unencrypted-at-rest at the destination, to a device that may be shared or backed up. The content policy (component + severity + threshold + runbook link; never account ids, order ids or key material) is therefore a *security control*, not a formatting preference.
2. **Metric labels as an inference channel.** `orders_total{state,env}` and `bybit_rate_remaining{account}` do not contain secrets but do reveal trading activity, account count and timing. Anyone who can reach `/metrics` can infer a good deal about positions. This is why the private-bind requirement is a control and why label content needs a rule, not a convention.

## Test plan
The model itself is a document; its verification is E04-X02's review and the abuse cases executed there and in E04-Q02 charter 3. Each control identified must name the test that proves it (unit, integration, ci-gate, drill, manual-review) per the verification-method column convention in `04-security-program.md` §6.

## Security notes
The threat-model document itself describes weaknesses and is therefore Internal-Confidential: it lives in the repository (private) and must not be included in any support bundle or public artefact.

## Accessibility notes

N/A, except that two identified DoS threats (log flood, cardinality explosion) have performance controls owned by E04-T02 and E04-T03 respectively.

SR-125's list of security-relevant metrics is cross-checked here for completeness and handed to E04-T03 for catalogue declaration.

title: Security review, abuse cases and SAST rules for logging, metrics and diagnostics
body:
## Context
Closes the security half of the epic's DoD: the STRIDE model from E04-X01 identified the threats; this ticket verifies that the shipped code actually resists them, and converts the durable properties into automated rules so they cannot silently regress once twenty more modules start logging. DoD §8 makes security sign-off non-optional for anything touching key handling — and the redaction filter is precisely the control standing between an API secret and a log file.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Abuse-case execution** against staging, from E04-X01's list:
  1. As a Manager and as a Viewer, attempt to read `/admin/health` detail, `/admin/incidents`, generate a support bundle and set a log-level override — all must 403 and be audited.
  2. Attempt to reach `/metrics`, Grafana, Prometheus and Alertmanager from outside the private network — all must be refused.
  3. Attempt log injection via `X-Correlation-Id`, via a symbol parameter, and via a telemetry payload field — none may alter the log field structure or forge another request's id.
  4. Attempt to smuggle a secret into a support bundle via a config value, a log line and an exception message — the pre-write scan must fail generation in all three cases.
  5. Attempt a cardinality explosion via the telemetry endpoint's `screen` field and via a symbol label — the guard must hold and the process must not OOM.
  6. Attempt a log flood via the runtime log-level override — TTL cap, namespace scoping and disk-guard must hold.
  7. Inspect a real alert notification payload for account ids, order ids or key material.
- **SAST/lint rules** (Semgrep + ESLint + ruff/bandit), merged into the CI ruleset from E03:
  - Ban `print()` and direct `logging.getLogger()` in application modules (must use the `cv.obs` logger factory).
  - Ban bare `asyncio.create_task` outside `cv.obs` (correlation loss).
  - Ban direct `prometheus_client` imports outside `cv.obs` (bypasses the registry, `env` label and cardinality guard).
  - Flag any f-string interpolation of a variable named like a secret into a log call (SR-120's "no free-form string interpolation").
  - Flag any new Prometheus label name not on the approved label allow-list.
  - Frontend: SR-127 rules already required (no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` without sanitiser) verified to cover the health-chrome components.
- **DAST**: an OWASP ZAP baseline pass against the api in staging, scoped to the observability endpoints (`/health/*`, `/admin/health`, `/admin/incidents`, `/admin/log-level`, `/telemetry/frontend`, `/admin/support-bundle`), with findings triaged.
- **Secrets-scanning verification**: confirm gitleaks covers `infra/grafana`, `infra/prometheus`, `infra/alertmanager` (dashboard and rule files are exactly where an embedded webhook token or datasource password gets committed by accident).
- **Permission/key checks**: verify log files and bundle output are `0600`/`0700`, that log directories are excluded from CI artefact upload (SR-124), and that the alert webhook secret is injected at runtime and absent from the repo and from images.
- Security sign-off comment on E04 and on each child ticket carrying the `security` label.

## Out of scope
- Penetration testing (E43, pre-R4 gate).
- Auth/RBAC implementation review (E09's own security tickets) — this ticket only verifies enforcement *on the observability endpoints*.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given every abuse case from E04-X01 is executed against staging
When results are recorded
Then each case either fails safely with the expected status code, audit row and no data disclosure, or is filed as a security Bug at priority/p0-critical or priority/p1-high

Given a developer adds a module that calls logging.getLogger() directly and logs an f-string containing api_secret
When CI runs
Then the Semgrep rules fail the build naming both violations, before review

Given a webhook token is committed into an Alertmanager config file in a scratch branch
When gitleaks runs in CI
Then the build fails and the secret is identified

Given the ZAP baseline scan completes against the observability endpoints
Then zero Critical/High findings remain unresolved, and any Medium has a dated accepted-risk entry per the R0 quality gate

Given a real Page-severity alert notification is captured
When its payload is inspected
Then it contains component, severity, threshold and runbook link, and contains no account id, order id, symbol-plus-size combination or key material
```

## Technical notes / design
The rules that matter most are the *structural* ones (ban the bypass) rather than the *pattern* ones (detect the bad string). A Semgrep rule that greps for "password" in log calls catches the careless case; a rule that forbids obtaining a logger outside the sanctioned factory makes the redaction filter unbypassable by construction. Prefer the latter, and allow-list the handful of legitimate exceptions explicitly with a comment convention rather than weakening the rule.

For the cardinality abuse case, run it against a process with a memory limit set so a failure is a clean OOM-kill in staging rather than an unbounded host-memory consumption — and assert the guard fires *before* memory grows, not that the process survives.

## Test plan
- Abuse cases executed manually against staging and, where automatable, converted into E2E tests added to the regression pack (E04-Q02) so they re-run forever.
- SAST rules unit-tested with positive and negative fixtures (a rule that never fires is as useless here as an alert that never fires).
- ZAP baseline wired as a scheduled CI job, not a one-off.
- Permission checks scripted and added to the deployment smoke test.

## Security notes
This ticket is the security verification for threats K1 (High), U5, D3 and asset A-17 from `04-security-program.md`. Findings are triaged per the R0 quality gate: zero Critical/High unresolved, Medium requires a dated accepted-risk entry. Any confirmed secret exposure triggers the exposure-assessment procedure (which environments, what retention, who had read access) and, if a live key is implicated, immediate rotation per SR key-rotation requirements.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — security verification. Any a11y defect noticed incidentally is filed with the `a11y` label against E04-D02.

## Performance notes
The cardinality and log-flood abuse cases double as performance-guard verification; record the measured behaviour (memory ceiling held, disk guard triggered) against the E04-T03/T02 controls.

## Observability
Confirms that SR-125's security-relevant metrics are exported and alerted on, and that `log_redactions_total` and `metric_cardinality_breach_total` are wired into the alert rule set as early-warning signals of a control being exercised.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every abuse case executed with recorded outcome; failures filed with priority and linked.
- [ ] SAST/lint rules merged into the CI ruleset with positive/negative fixtures and green.
- [ ] ZAP baseline job scheduled; findings triaged to the R0 gate.
- [ ] gitleaks coverage of `infra/**` verified by deliberate-commit test.
- [ ] File permissions and secret-injection checks scripted into the deployment smoke test.

**Sprint-window justification (Sprint 04 vs E04's declared window S02–S03).** `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` line 104/187 allocates E04 the window **S02–S03**, which prices and schedules the *engineering build*. This ticket reviews code delivered by `E04-T01..T06` and `E04-S02`, the last of which merges at the end of Sprint 03. A security review, abuse-case execution and SAST rule authoring can only assess merged artefacts — the support bundle, the alert payloads and the redaction filter must all exist before threats against them can be executed; the R0 SAST / SCA / secrets gate of `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §4.4 is a milestone gate, not a sprint-internal one. This is trailing verification, not build scope: it consumes no S02–S03 capacity, no other epic depends on its output before Sprint 05, and the R0 exit criteria it feeds are assessed at the R0 milestone at the end of Sprint 04.
